**Mapped cell evidence — Techniques, estimators and algorithms, Current**
- **Claim:** Current testing algorithms and measures include scenario-based test prioritization, open-/closed-loop benchmark evaluation, simulation/MIL/SIL/HIL execution, performance/incident metrics and safety-case traceability. ISO 34505 standardizes a traceable scenario-to-test-case process; it does not prescribe every scenario-generation algorithm. **Locator:** ISO 34505 official text; nuPlan benchmark and evaluation protocol; AVSC metrics; NHTSA incident reporting; ASAM XIL 3.0.0. **Sources:** D166-ISO-34505-PUBLISHED-2025, D166-NUPLAN-OFFICIAL-BENCHMARK, D166-AVSC-ADS-SAFETY-METRICS-2021, D166-NHTSA-ADS-CRASH-ORDER-2025, D166-ASAM-XIL-3-0-0 **Area context:** This connects test selection, execution and interpretation while emphasizing that open-loop prediction scores, closed-loop behavior, physical tests and crash outcomes measure different properties. **Limit:** nuPlan and AVSC have defined scopes and limitations; public ISO text is limited; crash counts lack complete exposure denominators; benchmarks do not demonstrate public-road safety. **Relationship:** Scenario criteria select tests; test benches execute cases; metrics quantify behavior and coverage; incidents/field data can reveal missing cases; the assurance argument explains what each measure can and cannot support.
- **Claim:** Safety-oriented MPC literature is grouped in the inspected 2025 author preprint into collision/risk mitigation, trajectory tracking/path following, and intersection/coordination, with nonlinear, robust, adaptive and learning-enhanced variants; the preprint itself flags scalability and computational-efficiency challenges. The later 2026 journal review's broader 101-study synthesis is visible only in publisher-indexed excerpts. **Locator:** Mahmood and Szabolcsi, Preprints.org v1 (2025), Abstract and Sections 2-3, full page opened; compare with Automation 2026, 7(3), 88 official publisher-indexed Abstract, Sections 2-6 and Table 5 excerpts. Do not transfer study totals between versions. **Sources:** D166-SAFETY-MPC-SYSTEMATIC-REVIEW-2026, D166-SAFETY-MPC-REVIEW-PREPRINT-2025 **Area context:** This provides a bounded map of contemporary safety-control technique families and validation caveats. It links safety V&V to planning/control evidence without turning any controller into a safety case or approval result. **Limit:** The 2026 publisher-indexed article text is extensive but not a complete independently inspected article. The 2025 source is an earlier non-peer-reviewed manuscript with internally differing study totals and is not equivalent to the version of record. Neither qualitative review provides independent efficacy evidence or establishes road-deployment safety. **Relationship:** {'type': 'complement', 'explanation': 'Safety-oriented MPC formulations complement system-level safety analysis and scenario/physical V&V; simulation results require validity, uncertainty and computational-feasibility checks before supporting operational claims.'}

**Mapped cell evidence — Techniques, estimators and algorithms, Emerging**
- **Claim:** Emerging techniques use search, fuzzing, reinforcement learning, retrieval-augmented or foundation-model generation to discover rare/high-risk scenarios. Any2Critical is a peer-reviewed example generating contextually related safety-critical cases from arbitrary real-world contexts; a 2026 IEEE survey separately catalogs LLM/VLM/multimodal/diffusion/world-model approaches and evaluation challenges. **Locator:** Any2Critical AAAI-26 full paper; IEEE Open Journal 2026 scenario-generation survey publisher abstract; NIST ongoing combinatorial coverage research; 2026 HSPG publisher abstract. **Sources:** D166-AAAI-ANY2CRITICAL-2026, D166-NIST-AUTONOMOUS-SYSTEMS-ASSURANCE, D166-SAFETY-CRITICAL-SCENARIO-SURVEY-PREPRINT-2026 **Area context:** These add data-driven and generative scenario discovery to established rule/knowledge-based test design, primarily as candidate generation and test prioritization paths. **Limit:** The AAAI paper's collision metric is not a safety score; IEEE evidence is abstract-only; NIST work is ongoing; scenario survey preprint is not peer-reviewed. Realism, distribution coverage and sim-to-real validity remain open. **Relationship:** Real-world context/data or specifications seed candidate scenarios; generation/search proposes cases; plausibility and coverage filters evaluate them; simulators/ADS produce outcomes; independent review and physical validation assess transfer.
- **Claim:** A 2026 research method evaluates scenario-set coverage across attribute ranges, ODD/behavior competencies, out-of-ODD cases and road-rule compliance, demonstrated on an ALKS case study; it is a proposed coverage analysis technique, not proof that a test set or ADS is safe. **Locator:** Chodowiec et al. (2026), IEEE Access 14, pp. 33117-33139; full PDF abstract and introduction, pages 0-2, lines 12-30 and 57-122; full paper methods/results in accessed PDF. **Sources:** D166-ODD-BEHAVIOR-SCENARIO-COVERAGE-2026 **Area context:** Technique analyzes scenario-set coverage relative to a specified system ODD and behavior competency; separate from generating the planner or executing physical tests. **Limit:** One peer-reviewed framework and ALKS case study; coverage dimensions do not prove exhaustive rare-event coverage, simulator validity, road performance or applicability to Nigerian traffic rules. **Relationship:** {'type': 'complement', 'explanation': 'Coverage analysis complements scenario generation and test execution by checking represented ranges and ODD/behavior dimensions; physical/on-road validation and an overall safety argument remain separate.'}

**Mapped cell evidence — Techniques, estimators and algorithms, Future**
- **Claim:** Future V&V research is moving toward integrated scenario-data lifecycles, input-space measurement, qualified virtual environments and risk-guided generation/prioritization. NIST describes an ongoing measurement framework; ISO/PAS 34506:2026 was published 2026-10-07; 2026 scenario reviews propose foundation-model and generative methods while identifying reliability and validation gaps. **Locator:** NIST Measurement Science for Automated Vehicles project page; ISO/PAS 34506:2026 official record; IEEE foundation-model scenario survey abstract; 2026 scenario database architecture paper abstract/full text. **Sources:** D166-NIST-AUTONOMOUS-SYSTEMS-ASSURANCE, D166-ISO-PAS-34506-VIRTUAL-TEST-ENVIRONMENTS-2026, D166-SAFETY-CRITICAL-SCENARIO-SURVEY-PREPRINT-2026, D166-AAAI-ANY2CRITICAL-2026 **Area context:** These are research and standardization directions for making scenario evidence more measurable, reusable, risk-targeted and tied to virtual-environment quality. **Limit:** NIST project remains ongoing; ISO PAS is under publication; preprint/survey claims and individual generative results need validation. No universal complete assurance pipeline has been demonstrated. **Relationship:** Scenario databases and generative/search techniques may produce prioritized tests; environment qualification and independent model validation bound test meaning; evidence still requires traceability, physical checks and residual-risk reasoning.
- **Claim:** CoCoSaFe is a research-stage offline code-level verification method combining ODD/behavior formalization, compositional contracts, controlled-invariant safe sets and bounded model checking for traditional ACC/LKA controller code, with a BMC/neural-verifier decomposition for DNN controllers. It is one formal-assurance frontier candidate, not an accepted certification method or full-ADS safety case. **Locator:** Nenchev et al., Journal of Systems and Software 230 (2025), 112499, published PDF: https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/document/3553193; method Sections 4.1-4.3.2 (pp. 3-8), evaluation Section 5 (pp. 8-10), validity/future work Section 6 (pp. 11-12), DOI 10.1016/j.jss.2025.112499. **Sources:** D166-NENCHEV-COCOSAFE-CODE-LEVEL-VERIFICATION-2025 **Area context:** Future/futuristic frontier candidate because this recent peer-reviewed method remains research-stage and the authors identify broader ODD/controller evaluation as future work; horizon is a maturity classification, not a prediction of adoption. **Limit:** One study with no physical vehicle/public-road validation, full ADS assurance, tool qualification, regulator acceptance, certification or independent replication. Authors note the need for complementary data-driven testing and future urban/adverse-weather/other-controller studies; formal results remain conditional on specification/model/tool assumptions. **Relationship:** {'type': 'complement', 'explanation': 'Formal controller-code verification can complement scenario/data-driven testing and broader safety-case evidence by checking code against a modeled safe set; neither method subsumes the other, and this paper does not establish a complete ADS safety case.'}

**Mapped cell evidence — Tools, software and data, Traditional**
- **Claim:** The ASAM archive documents an established HIL/XIL test-automation interface lineage: HIL V1.0.0 in 2009, followed by XIL releases through V2.2.0 in 2020. This is evidence of a versioned testbench-interface standard family, not proof of ADS-specific adoption or safety effectiveness. **Locator:** ASAM XIL - Previous Releases archive, lines 145-219 (HIL V1.0.0, 22 June 2009; XIL V2.0.0-2.2.0, 2013-2020); current ASAM XIL datasheet/overview, lines 145-200, defining the Generic Simulator Interface and its test-automation/MIL-SIL-HIL scope. **Sources:** D166-ASAM-XIL-HISTORY-2009-2020, D166-ASAM-XIL-3-0-0 **Area context:** Established/traditional testbench interface lineage for hardware/software/model-in-the-loop automation; this is the historical standard/tool-interface context, not an ADS simulator, dataset or safety validation result. **Limit:** Release listings do not prove implementation prevalence, ADS-specific use, conformance, simulator fidelity, scenario coverage or safety effectiveness. Full historical specifications and actual deployment were not inspected; member access/pricing terms are not evidence of public implementation. **Relationship:** {'type': 'complement', 'explanation': 'A testbench API complements simulators, ECUs and test automation by defining an interface boundary; it does not itself supply the simulator, test scenarios, validity evidence or safety argument.'}

**Mapped cell evidence — Tools, software and data, Current**
- **Claim:** Current validation tooling in this evidence set includes CARLA simulation, nuPlan benchmark/data/evaluation, ASAM OSI simulation messages and XIL test-automation interfaces, plus competition-defined logging/test signals. These tools and data support different layers and are not interchangeable. **Locator:** CARLA official docs; nuPlan benchmark docs; ASAM OSI 3.8.0/XIL 3.0.0; Formula Student Germany Driverless Specification 2026 v1.1. **Sources:** D166-CARLA-SIMULATOR-INTRO, D166-NUPLAN-OFFICIAL-BENCHMARK, D166-ASAM-OSI-3-8-0, D166-ASAM-XIL-3-0-0, D166-FSG-DRIVERLESS-SPEC-2026-V1-1 **Area context:** CARLA/nuPlan enable virtual scenario and benchmark work; OSI exchanges selected simulation data; XIL connects test automation to MIL/SIL/HIL benches; event specs define test/log interfaces for their own competition. **Limit:** No simulator is validated for every ODD; benchmark performance is not safety proof; OSI/XIL are interface standards, not complete test suites; competition specs are not public-road requirements. **Relationship:** Datasets/scenarios enter simulators and test harnesses; interfaces connect models and test benches; results and logs feed metrics, defect analysis and assurance records.
- **Claim:** nuPlan, ASAM interfaces and scenario-evaluation standards support repeatable benchmark or virtual evidence; ISO/PAS 34506:2026 specifies qualification of virtual test environments for open- and closed-loop testing, not individual simulator-model accuracy or ADS performance. **Locator:** nuPlan Planning Benchmark documentation; ISO 34502:2022, ISO 34505:2025 and ISO/PAS 34506:2026 catalogue records; ASAM OSI/Scenario source-index records. **Sources:** D166-NUPLAN-OFFICIAL-BENCHMARK, D166-ASAM-OSI-3-8-0, D166-ISO-34502-SCENARIO-SAFETY-EVALUATION-2022, D166-ISO-PAS-34506-VIRTUAL-TEST-ENVIRONMENTS-2026 **Area context:** Simulation/benchmark methods form one layer within a broader V&V evidence strategy. **Limit:** ISO/PAS 34506:2026 qualifies a virtual test environment, but explicitly does not assess individual simulator-model accuracy or ADS performance. Simulator models, scenario distributions, sensor/vehicle fidelity and coverage still limit inference; no qualification implies road performance. **Relationship:** {'type': 'complement', 'explanation': 'Virtual testing complements but does not replace closed-course, on-road, system-level and approval evidence.'}

**Mapped cell evidence — Tools, software and data, Emerging**
- **Claim:** Emerging scenario-safety data/tools include Any2Critical's NHTSA-5K-based context/scenario method, NIST's ongoing combinatorial input-space measurement work, and newly specified virtual-test-environment qualification under ISO/PAS 34506; NVIDIA SAFE is a vendor example of an integrated evidence ecosystem. **Locator:** AAAI Any2Critical paper; NIST project pages; ISO/PAS 34506:2026 official record; NVIDIA Halos SAFE technical brief. **Sources:** D166-AAAI-ANY2CRITICAL-2026, D166-NIST-AUTONOMOUS-SYSTEMS-ASSURANCE, D166-ISO-PAS-34506-VIRTUAL-TEST-ENVIRONMENTS-2026, D166-NVIDIA-HALOS-SAFE-TECHNICAL-BRIEF **Area context:** These extend standard simulator/benchmark toolchains with targeted scenario data/generation, coverage measurement and environment qualification or multi-source safety-evidence integration. **Limit:** NIST is ongoing research; PAS is published; Any2Critical is one study; NVIDIA is commercially interested vendor material. None is a universal completed toolchain or independent safety certification. **Relationship:** Scenario/context data and generation tools feed virtual testing; coverage measurement and environment qualification characterize the test basis; results may join simulation, road and fleet evidence under an explicit claim.
- **Claim:** TARGET is an emerging research toolchain that converts traffic-rule text into a validated functional-scenario DSL, instantiates simulator-specific scripts, and records ADS behavior for violation analysis. Its authors report testing seven ADSs with 284 scenarios derived from 54 rules across CARLA, LGSVL and MetaDrive, surfacing 610 issues; two were confirmed by developers. This is research evidence, not proof of tool adoption or ADS safety. **Locator:** Deng et al., IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 51(7), 2025, pp. 1950-1968; arXiv:2305.06018v4 full HTML: framework/DSL §§III-A-B, rule parsing/validation §III-C, script synthesis §III-D, monitor §III-E, experiments §§IV-V, validity threats §VII, future direction §VIII; official open-source repository README and scenario DSL example. **Sources:** D166-TARGET-TRAFFIC-RULE-TEST-GENERATION-2025 **Area context:** Emerging research toolchain for rule-derived simulation tests and ADS issue discovery; publication and open-source code do not establish commercial use, standards conformity or safety acceptance. **Limit:** One research framework; simulated evaluations across seven selected ADSs and 54 rules, not a representative fleet or exhaustive traffic-rule set. Only two findings were developer-confirmed; issue counts are not incidence rates, real-world safety effects or approval evidence. Traffic-rule scope, map coverage, simulator fidelity, geographic/legal variation, model versioning, reproducibility and current maintenance require independent review. **Relationship:** {'type': 'complement', 'explanation': 'Rule-derived scenario generation complements formal scenario specifications, scenario libraries, runtime monitors and physical validation; it does not replace those independent assurance layers.'}

**Mapped cell evidence — Tools, software and data, Future**
- **Claim:** Future tool candidates include foundation-model-driven scenario generation/analysis, living scenario databases and integrated virtual-test qualification/evidence frameworks. Current evidence includes a peer-reviewed 2026 survey, an open Any2Critical research implementation/paper, NIST's ongoing measurement work, ISO/PAS 34506 is published and a vendor SAFE framework. **Locator:** IEEE 2026 scenario foundation-model survey abstract; AAAI Any2Critical proceedings; NIST ongoing project; ISO/PAS 34506 official status; NVIDIA SAFE technical brief. **Sources:** D166-IEEE-FOUNDATION-MODELS-SCENARIO-SURVEY-2026, D166-AAAI-ANY2CRITICAL-2026, D166-NIST-AUTONOMOUS-SYSTEMS-ASSURANCE, D166-ISO-PAS-34506-VIRTUAL-TEST-ENVIRONMENTS-2026, D166-NVIDIA-HALOS-SAFE-TECHNICAL-BRIEF **Area context:** These indicate possible next-generation tooling for generating, curating, qualifying and measuring scenario evidence, while maintaining distinct generation, simulation, model-validity and safety-argument functions. **Limit:** Survey abstract and vendor framework are limited evidence; NIST and ISO work are ongoing/under publication; no unified future tool has independently demonstrated comprehensive AV safety. **Relationship:** Future scenario tools could connect source data, generation, qualification and evaluation; test results would still require independent coverage and physical/operational evidence.
- **Claim:** ScenicProver is a research-stage software framework built on Scenic that supports component/interface modeling, assume-guarantee contracts, simulator-based probabilistic verification, Lean 4 proof integration, evidence composition and automatic assurance-case generation. The paper demonstrates the tool on simulated AEB; it does not establish code availability beyond its statement that case-study code is in a repository, tool qualification, deployment or safety approval. **Locator:** Vin et al., arXiv:2511.02164v1, full HTML §§1, 3-6 and Appendix 0.C; framework capabilities and Lean 4 integration lines 61-85; implementation details lines 226-230; authors state full AEB code is in a repository at lines 310-314. **Sources:** D166-SCENICPROVER-COMPOSITIONAL-VERIFICATION-2025 **Area context:** A research software framework for integrated evidence management over learning-enabled ADS components; future/futuristic describes its research-stage scope, not verified future adoption. **Limit:** Preprint research implementation; no independent installation/build, tool qualification or external user/adoption evidence inspected. AEB case is simulated and simplified; no physical vehicle or road validation. Formal and probabilistic outputs depend on modeled environment and supplied contracts/assumptions; tool output is not itself a safety certificate. **Relationship:** {'type': 'complement', 'explanation': 'The framework can organize proof and testing artifacts for an assurance case, complementing scenario-generation, safety-case review and physical V&V tools; it does not replace their evidence or acceptance.'}

**Mapped cell evidence — Standards, credentials and learning resources, Traditional**
- **Claim:** Two foundational international standards distinguish different automotive safety problem classes: ISO 26262:2018 addresses hazards from malfunctioning safety-related E/E systems across the vehicle lifecycle, while ISO 21448:2022 (SOTIF) addresses unreasonable risk from functional insufficiencies and reasonably foreseeable misuse in intended functions that depend on situational awareness. Their scopes are complementary, not interchangeable; both are published editions marked by ISO as to be revised, and neither alone is ADS approval or proof of safety. **Locator:** ISO 26262 official series record https://www.iso.org/publication/PUB200262.html and ISO 26262-1:2018, -2:2018, -4:2018 catalogue abstracts; ISO 21448:2022 official catalogue https://www.iso.org/standard/77490.html, abstract/exclusions and lifecycle stage 90.92 ('to be revised'). Public catalogue records only; normative text not inspected. **Sources:** D166-ISO-26262, D166-ISO-21448-2022-STATUS-SCOPE **Area context:** Established foundational international safety standards for road-vehicle E/E systems and intended-function safety; standards are distinct by hazard scope and are not a complete ADS safety case or regulatory approval framework. **Limit:** Only official public catalogue abstracts/status were inspected, not full normative clauses; no conformity or certification conclusion can be made. ISO 26262 addresses malfunctioning E/E behavior and does not address nominal performance; ISO 21448 excludes ISO 26262 faults and cybersecurity and is not intended for functions with established trusted V&V measures. Both cited editions are marked 'to be revised'; draft/replacement content and national adoption were not reviewed. Neither is a standalone ADS approval or full safety-case standard. **Relationship:** {'type': 'complement', 'explanation': 'ISO 26262 and ISO 21448 address different but potentially interacting hazard classes; ADS-level safety-case, cybersecurity, scenario/ODD validation and regulatory requirements remain separate evidence and applicability questions.'}

**Mapped cell evidence — Standards, credentials and learning resources, Current**
- **Claim:** Current safety standards/regulation relevant to ADS V&V include ISO 26262 (functional safety), ISO 21448/SOTIF, ISO 34502/34503, published ISO 34505:2025, UL 4600, U.S. NHTSA voluntary guidance, ASAM OSI/XIL and ALKS-specific UN R157. Their scopes differ; none is a universal credential or a complete safety proof. **Locator:** Official ISO/UL/NHTSA/UNECE/ASAM records and texts; current ISO 34505 publication-status correction; reviewed 2026-10-23 through 2026-10-26. **Sources:** D166-ISO-26262, D166-ISO-21448, D166-ISO-34502-SCENARIO-SAFETY-EVALUATION-2022, D166-ISO-34503-ODD-TAXONOMY-2023, D166-ISO-34505-PUBLISHED-2025, D166-UL4600-ED3-AUTONOMOUS-SAFETY-2023, D166-NHTSA-ADS-VOLUNTARY-GUIDANCE-CURRENT, D166-ASAM-OSI-3-8-0, D166-ASAM-XIL-3-0-0, D166-UNECE-UNR157-AMENDMENT-4-2023 **Area context:** This provides an organized standards/resource map for safety case, ODD, scenario testing, simulation interfaces and jurisdiction-specific approval study. **Limit:** Full ISO texts are paid and clause-level review is incomplete; NHTSA guidance is voluntary/U.S.-specific; UN R157 is ALKS-only and adoption-specific; UL 4600 is voluntary. Standards do not certify a learner or prove a system safe. **Relationship:** Select standards based on product/function, hazards, lifecycle and jurisdiction; use ODD/safety frameworks and scenario/test standards with simulation interfaces as applicable; preserve compliance evidence and limits.
- **Claim:** NHTSA describes its ADS guidance and VSSA submissions as voluntary; UNECE records WP.29's June 2026 adoption and October 2026 publication of UN GTR No. 26 on ADS, while the parallel UN Regulation and national implementation remain distinct legal-status questions. **Locator:** NHTSA ADS FAQ (voluntary guidance/VSSA); UNECE WP.29 June 2026 adoption status and Global Technical Regulations registry entry ECE/TRANS/180/Add.26, dated 1 October 2026; selected final-text passages surfaced in UNECE document search. **Sources:** D166-NHTSA-ADS-VOLUNTARY-GUIDANCE-CURRENT, D166-UNECE-UNR157-AMENDMENT-4-2023, D166-UNECE-UN-GTR-26-REGISTRY-2026 **Area context:** Regulatory/approval context is jurisdiction-, vehicle- and use-case-specific; distinguish guidance, regulation, draft and voluntary disclosure. **Limit:** The complete GTR PDF and UN Regulation No. 185 treaty record were not directly reviewed; indexed GTR excerpts support only a high-level scope claim. No Nigerian incorporation, enforceability or compliance is inferred. **Relationship:** {'type': 'context_only', 'explanation': 'These sources set jurisdictional/deployment context rather than prescribing a technical planner or general engineering credential.'}
- **Claim:** UNECE reports that WP.29 adopted a new UN Regulation and UN Global Technical Regulation on Automated Driving Systems in June 2026. This adds a global ADS-level regulatory framework to the existing function- and jurisdiction-specific standards landscape; the adopted status is not equivalent to entry into force or local implementation everywhere. **Locator:** UNECE WP.29/GRVA official status page, June 2026 entry; official proposal records ECE/TRANS/WP.29/2026/137 and /139. **Sources:** D166-UNECE-ADS-REGULATION-2026 **Area context:** Safety/V&V curricula need to distinguish system-level ADS approval evidence and regulatory safety management from component functional-safety, SOTIF, scenario-test and virtual-environment qualification methods. **Limit:** Summary and proposal records support the adoption/work-programme status only. Entry-into-force dates, contracting-party adoption, detailed requirements and Nigerian domestic legal effect are not inferred. **Relationship:** Applicable ADS regulation -> manufacturer safety-management and safety-case evidence -> authority assessment and confirmatory testing under the applicable rule. This is a jurisdiction-dependent governance/output relation, not a universal prerequisite between learning items.

**Mapped cell evidence — Standards, credentials and learning resources, Emerging**
- **Claim:** A current emerging standards development is published ISO/PAS 34506:2026, which defines qualification criteria/procedures for virtual test environments across open/closed loop and MiL/SiL examples, with possible HiL/ViL extensions. It explicitly does not validate individual simulation models or the ADS. **Locator:** Official ISO/PAS 34506 record and lifecycle status inspected 2026-10-26; compare with published ISO 34505:2025 and ASAM XIL/OSI scope. **Sources:** D166-ISO-PAS-34506-VIRTUAL-TEST-ENVIRONMENTS-2026, D166-ISO-34505-PUBLISHED-2025, D166-ASAM-XIL-3-0-0, D166-ASAM-OSI-3-8-0 **Area context:** This adds a distinct emerging learning topic: qualification of the virtual test environment itself, adjacent to scenario/test-case standards and simulator interfaces. **Limit:** The PAS was published at stage 60.60 on 2026-10-07 and public abstract only; qualification does not validate individual sensor/vehicle models or the ADS itself. **Relationship:** Test scenarios execute in a virtual test environment; environment qualification assesses whether that environment is fit for intended evaluation; model validation and ADS evaluation remain separate obligations.
- **Claim:** ISO/PAS 34506:2026 is a newly published specification for qualifying virtual test environments for open- and closed-loop ADS testing; its qualification scope explicitly excludes individual simulator-model accuracy and ADS performance. **Locator:** ISO/PAS 34506:2026 official catalogue record, published 2026-10-07, https://www.iso.org/standard/89865.html. **Sources:** D166-ISO-PAS-34506-VIRTUAL-TEST-ENVIRONMENTS-2026 **Area context:** An emerging virtual V&V qualification framework; neither publication age nor catalogue scope proves adoption or legal force. **Limit:** Does not establish simulator-model validity, ADS safety/performance, scenario completeness, road transfer, regulatory approval, adoption or credential requirements; full normative text and implementation evidence were not reviewed. **Relationship:** {'type': 'complement', 'explanation': 'Environment qualification is one virtual V&V layer and complements, but does not replace, model validation, ADS-performance assessment, physical/on-road evidence or jurisdictional approval.'}

**Mapped cell evidence — Outputs and downstream role context, Emerging**
- **Claim:** Emerging V&V outputs include generated critical-scenario libraries with provenance, scenario coverage and virtual-environment qualification records, integrated simulator/bench data and test evidence that can be traced into safety arguments. Any2Critical provides one research example; ISO/PAS 34506 and NIST describe standardization/research directions. **Locator:** AAAI Any2Critical 2026; ISO/PAS 34506:2026 official scope; NIST Autonomous Systems Assurance and Measurement Science projects; conditional validation-role evidence. **Sources:** D166-AAAI-ANY2CRITICAL-2026, D166-ISO-PAS-34506-VIRTUAL-TEST-ENVIRONMENTS-2026, D166-NIST-AUTONOMOUS-SYSTEMS-ASSURANCE, D166-GM-AUTONOMY-EVALUATION-2026, D166-WAYMO-SOFTWARE-QUALITY-SAFETY-OPERATIONS-2026 **Area context:** These artifacts may support scenario curation, test prioritization and evidence-quality assessment for validation and safety-analysis assignments. **Limit:** Generative scenarios and qualification records do not establish sufficient coverage or real-world safety; NIST work is ongoing; role evidence remains task-conditional, and no D166 routes are added. **Relationship:** Real-world data/specifications and ODD inform scenario generation; generated cases are checked for plausibility and coverage; qualified environments execute tests; coverage/evaluation and residual risk are communicated to safety and release roles.
- **Claim:** California's adopted 2026 AV rules define structured regulator-facing reporting outputs for dynamic-driving-task-relevant system failures, driverless vehicle immobilizations, public-road vehicle miles traveled, specified hard-braking events and AV traffic noncompliance, with prescribed electronic templates and reporting cadences. These are jurisdiction-specific oversight artifacts, not evidence that an ADS passed V&V or is safe. **Locator:** California DMV adopted Article 3.7 §§227.56, 227.58, 227.60, 227.66 and 227.68; official index https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles/california-autonomous-vehicle-regulations/, adopted PDF https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/file/order-to-adopt-article-3-7-regulations-pdf/, template portal https://qr.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles/autonomous-vehicles-program-permit-resources/. NHTSA SGO data/limitations: https://www.nhtsa.gov/laws-regulations/standing-general-order-crash-reporting. **Sources:** D166-CA-DMV-AV-REPORTING-RULES-2026, D166-NHTSA-ADS-CRASH-ORDER-2025 **Area context:** Emerging 2026 regulator-defined operational monitoring/reporting outputs for ADS in California, with NHTSA's separately scoped U.S. federal crash-reporting data as contextual complement. Adoption is established; some reporting provisions are phased/operative after specified delay. **Limit:** California-only legal scope; reporting sections are phased and Article 3.7 specifies a 120-day delay after effective date, so this mapping does not assert every requirement was already operative on access date. NHTSA data are not exposure-normalized and may be incomplete or reporting-awareness biased. Reporting is not a safety finding, certification, proof of comprehensive coverage or a universal global practice; no Nigerian or UNECE equivalence is claimed. **Relationship:** {'type': 'complement', 'explanation': 'Operational incident/exposure reports complement design-time and test-time V&V evidence by supporting regulator monitoring and follow-up; they do not replace scenario, physical-test, safety-case or type-approval evidence.'}

**Mapped cell evidence — Outputs and downstream role context, Future**
- **Claim:** UNECE's ADS 22nd-session document index lists an EC presentation titled Safety Performance Indicators (ADS-22-22r1), dated 7 Oct 2026, alongside an ADS2 IWG 2027 planning presentation (ADS-22-24). These are identifiable emerging regulator-facing evidence/planning artifacts, but underlying contents and future deliverables were not inspected; the record does not establish adopted indicators, required reporting schemas or future safety outcomes. **Locator:** Accessible secondary record for ADS-22-22/Rev.1: https://globalautoregs.com/documents/43758, lines 152-180; official UNECE index identifies linked presentation, direct fetch returned 403. **Sources:** D166-UNECE-ADS22-SAFETY-INDICATORS-AND-ADS2-PLAN-2026 **Area context:** Emerging regulator-session research artifact with prospective field-data follow-up; not an adopted standard or operationally validated output. **Limit:** Secondary summary only; underlying presentation/methods unavailable, with no independent result, adopted metrics, mandatory schema or operational safety effect established. **Relationship:** {'type': 'context_only', 'explanation': 'The registry summary describes evidence candidates for in-service monitoring, but does not establish adoption or a required regulator/role deliverable.'}

#### Current area records

- **Vehicle Sensing and Sensor Calibration** (`D166:vehicle-sensing-and-sensor-calibration`): Acquire, synchronize, calibrate and preprocess sensor signals and maintain the sensor hardware/data interfaces used by automated-driving systems.

## D011 conditional role-to-area task evidence

These are source-backed examples for selected D011 routes. They do not create canonical role-area routes or change role fit. Each cited card is attached to the same role record named in the row; only the task conditions stated here are supported.

- **middle office analyst → Quantitative Financial Risk Modeling** — Useful when an OTC derivatives middle-office assignment includes collateral, exposure-related reconciliations, trade-break analysis, data-quality checks or model controls and reporting that support financial-risk measurement and governance. **Boundary:** Amundi's employer posting supports operational/control work around derivatives and risk-model inputs; it does not establish that a middle-office analyst develops or owns quantitative risk models, sets risk policy or performs every market/credit/liquidity calculation. **Evidence:** [D011-AMUNDI-OTC-MIDDLE-OFFICE-2026](https://jobs.amundi.com/job/job-otc-middle-office-analyst-m-f_115102.aspx)

This supports a conditional bridge from mathematical research to financial-risk modeling, not a claim that mathematicians generally work in finance or that all risk methods are required. **Evidence:** [D011-ONET-MATHEMATICIAN-2026](https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/15-2021.00); [D011-BLACKROCK-FIXED-INCOME-RISK-MATH-2026](https://careers.blackrock.com/job/new-york/associate-fixed-income-risk-management/45831/99769538576)

## D011 financial-risk role-task dispositions

All 22 stored links into the risk-modeling area now have an explicit task disposition. These are conditional user, contributor or specialist task contexts; they do not claim that every listed occupation develops risk models.

- **foreign exchange trader** — `conditional_task_supported`. Useful when the trader monitors currency positions and market drivers, reports exposures/results or devises trading and hedge strategies that consume quantitative risk estimates. **Boundary:** O*NET groups diverse sales/trading titles and supports these tasks at occupational-profile level; this is a conditional risk-output/user link, not evidence that every FX trader builds risk models or performs enterprise risk management. **Evidence:** [D011-ONET-41-3031.00](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/41-3031.00)
- **securities analyst** — `conditional_task_supported`. Directly relevant for an equity/securities analyst assignment that quantifies credit or market exposure, develops risk-assessment models, analyzes severe-market scenarios or reports risk positions. **Boundary:** O*NET's Financial Risk Specialists profile lists Securities Analyst and Equity Research Analyst among sample titles and includes these explicit tasks, while the Financial and Investment Analysts profile covers broader valuation and forecasting. This is a task-specific route and does not make every securities analyst a risk specialist. **Evidence:** [D011-ONET-13-2054.00](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/13-2054.00); [D011-ONET-13-2051.00](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/13-2051.00)
- **mergers and acquisitions analyst** — `conditional_task_supported`.
