## D011 named-technique comparisons and relationships

These source-backed comparisons describe technique distinctions, alternatives, complements and claim limits for later graph review. They are not canonical items, student-display approvals, or graph/sequence edges.

- **Correlation techniques: Pearson, Spearman and Kendall** Ã¢â‚¬â€ They are related association measures but not interchangeable alternatives: Pearson targets product-moment/linear association under its inferential assumptions, while Spearman and Kendall use ranks and answer rank-association questions. Pick according to the estimand, data scale, dependence structure and assumptions; finance time-series autocorrelation and nonstationarity still need separate handling. **Sources:** [D011-R-CORRELATION-TESTS](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/cor.test.html) **Limit:** R documentation establishes implementation choices and stated assumptions, not finance-task prevalence or the suitability of an individual correlation screen.
- **Categorical/count inference: Pearson chi-square and Fisher exact test** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Both can test association in contingency tables, but their inferential setup differs. Pearson chi-square uses an asymptotic reference distribution (and offers Monte Carlo p-values); Fisher conditions on fixed margins and computes exact probabilities when feasible. Expected counts, table structure, margins and computational size guide comparison. Neither is a universal replacement for the other. **Sources:** [D011-R-CHI-SQUARE-TEST](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/chisq.test.html); [D011-R-FISHER-EXACT-TEST](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/fisher.test.html) **Limit:** These are count-data association/goodness-of-fit procedures, not continuous-outcome regression or numeric finance-return tests; domain relevance depends on a categorical/count task.
- **Linear regression, ANOVA and ANCOVA** Ã¢â‚¬â€ A one-stratum ANOVA or ANCOVA can be represented within a linear-model framework, while the question, factor coding, design, contrasts and inferential interpretation differ. ANOVA is not a separate universal prerequisite after regression; it is a related analysis for comparisons of means/model terms under a specified design. **Sources:** [D011-R-LM-ANOVA-ANCOVA](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/lm.html); [D011-STATSMODELS-REGRESSION-FAMILY](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/regression.html) **Limit:** Software documentation demonstrates shared model machinery, not equivalence of research questions or assumptions. Time-series and panel dependence require suitable covariance/error handling.
- **Regression choices by outcome form: OLS versus logistic/probit/count models** Ã¢â‚¬â€ OLS is a linear conditional-mean model commonly used for numeric outcomes; binary Logit/Probit models use a binary response and link; Poisson/negative-binomial models address count outcomes. The response scale and estimand drive the choice. These are model-family alternatives under different data-generating and decision questions, not tool substitutes or a single compulsory chain. **Sources:** [D011-R-LM-ANOVA-ANCOVA](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/lm.html); [D011-R-GLM-BINARY-LOGISTIC](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/glm.html); [D011-STATSMODELS-DISCRETE-RESPONSE](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/discretemod.html) **Limit:** This index does not adjudicate causal interpretation, rare-event performance, overdispersion, or a specific finance dataset; each needs method and task-specific evidence.
- **Traditional econometrics and machine learning in asset pricing** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Finance research compares parsimonious regression benchmarks with regularization/dimension reduction and flexible tree/neural-network models. The reviewed study attributes some predictive gains to nonlinear predictor interactions unavailable to simpler specifications, but higher flexibility increases overfitting risk. Its U.S.-equity results are evidence that ML can extend familiar regression benchmarks for a defined task, not evidence of universal superiority or a required replacement. **Sources:** [D011-RFS-ML-ASSET-PRICING-2020](https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhaa009); [D011-WILEY-ASSET-PRICING-ML-REVIEW-2024](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/joes.12532) **Limit:** Task, predictor set, period, market and evaluation design bound these findings; compare against robust baselines and current evidence before mapping method dependencies.
- **Model evaluation for financial prediction and strategy selection** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Generic ML model selection provides fitting, validation and cross-validation tools, but financial time-series validation must respect chronology; scikit-learn explicitly distinguishes time-dependent data from i.i.d. folds and provides future-only TimeSeriesSplit with conditions. Separately, PBO/CSCV addresses selection overfit among many backtested strategy configurations. These methods answer related but different validation questions and can complement an untouched out-of-sample test and economic cost analysis. **Sources:** [D011-SCIKIT-MODEL-EVALUATION](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/model_selection.html); [D011-SCIKIT-TIME-SERIES-SPLIT](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/cross_validation.html); [D011-RFS-ML-ASSET-PRICING-2020](https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhaa009); [D011-PBO-BACKTEST-OVERFIT-2017](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/4w1110bb) **Limit:** No single evaluation method proves a strategy will work live. Label overlap, information leakage, transaction costs, capacity, multiple trials and regime change require explicit handling. These notes are evidence for graph review, not graph edges.
- **Time-series mean dynamics and conditional-volatility models are separate, composable choices** Ã¢â‚¬â€ AR/ARIMA/VAR and related models describe conditional means or joint dynamics and handle trend, stationarity, seasonality and cross-series relationships. ARCH/GARCH-family models describe changing conditional variance, often attached to a mean equation after residual diagnostics show volatility clustering. They can be combined; GARCH is not a substitute for ARIMA or VAR, and an AR model is not a volatility model. Forecast target and diagnostics decide whether either layer is useful. **Sources:** [D011-STATSMODELS-TIME-SERIES-2026](https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/tsa); [D011-CFA-TIMESERIES-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/time-series-analysis); [D011-ARCH-VOLATILITY-PROCESSES-2026](https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/stable/univariate/volatility.html) **Limit:** Software API and curriculum establish the model families and teaching context, not universal modeling practice. The choice and ordering depend on data frequency, target, assumptions and residual evidence; this is conceptual composition, not a learner prerequisite edge.
- **Conditional variance alternatives: ARCH/GARCH variants, EWMA and RiskMetrics** Ã¢â‚¬â€ ARCH/GARCH variants model conditional variance from past innovations and variance; asymmetric EGARCH, GJR/TARCH or APARCH forms can express sign/asymmetry or power responses, while FIGARCH/HARCH/MIDAS variants address different persistence/aggregation structures. EWMA/RiskMetrics are simpler parameterized or fixed-weight variance processes and may serve as baselines or operational alternatives. These choices answer a variance-estimation/forecast question; use residual diagnostics, distribution assumptions, horizon and evaluation loss to compare them. **Sources:** [D011-ARCH-VOLATILITY-PROCESSES-2026](https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/stable/univariate/volatility.html); [D011-ARCH-UNIVARIATE-MODELS-2026](https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/stable/univariate/univariate.html); [D011-CFA-HYPOTHESIS-TESTS-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/hypothesis-testing) **Limit:** The arch documentation lists available forms, not their universal suitability. It does not fully cover stochastic volatility or every multivariate conditional-covariance method; these must be compared separately when the task needs them.
- **GARCH versus genuine stochastic volatility** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Both represent time-varying volatility but their variance dynamics differ. Standard GARCH is observation-driven, conditioning variance on observed returns/shocks; genuine stochastic-volatility models add a latent volatility innovation, making inference and estimation more complex but connecting naturally to continuous-time asset-pricing models. Empirical comparisons do not establish one winner for every asset or horizon. They are related model families whose suitability depends on data, inference and pricing/risk output, not a mandatory chain. **Sources:** [D011-CHICAGO-FED-STOCHASTIC-VOLATILITY-2009](https://www.chicagofed.org/publications/working-papers/2009/wp-04); [D011-JFUTURES-GARCH-IMPLIED-REALIZED-2016](https://www.storre.stir.ac.uk/handle/1893/23189); [D011-ARCH-VOLATILITY-PROCESSES-2026](https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/stable/univariate/volatility.html) **Limit:** The Chicago Fed paper is a 2009 conceptual review and the applied comparison is one 2016 stock-index study. Validate current methods and market-specific performance; implementation availability alone does not establish route fit.
- **Daily returns, option-implied volatility and high-frequency realized volatility** Ã¢â‚¬â€ These are different information sources and targets. Return-based GARCH estimates conditional variance from past returns; implied volatility is option-price-derived and forward-looking under pricing assumptions; realized volatility measures variation from intraday returns and can itself become a time series for AR/VAR/HAR-style forecasting. Sources report that combinations or relative rankings vary by horizon, proxy, loss function and market; realized and implied measures can add information rather than simply replace GARCH. **Sources:** [D011-JFUTURES-GARCH-IMPLIED-REALIZED-2016](https://www.storre.stir.ac.uk/handle/1893/23189); [D011-NBER-REALIZED-VOL-2001](https://www.nber.org/papers/w8160); [D011-CORSI-HAR-RV-2009](https://doi.org/10.1093/jjfinec/nbp001) **Limit:** Proxy construction, microstructure noise, option liquidity, sampling frequency and forecast horizon materially affect results. The cited comparisons are bounded historical markets and do not justify a universal choice or direct sequence edge.
- **HAR, long-memory/regime econometrics and ML for realized-volatility forecasts** Ã¢â‚¬â€ HAR-RV aggregates realized volatility across daily, weekly and monthly horizons as a parsimonious, long-memory-like baseline; ARFIMA and threshold/smooth-transition/Markov-switching variants model different persistence or regime behavior. XGBoost and neural networks offer more flexible nonlinear alternatives and can benefit from richer predictors, but two recent comparisons show no systematic ML win over the broader econometric set; forecast winner depends on horizon, predictor set and statistical versus economic objective. ML can test nonlinear extensions without replacing traditional baselines by default. **Sources:** [D011-CORSI-HAR-RV-2009](https://doi.org/10.1093/jjfinec/nbp001); [D011-FED-REALIZED-VOL-ML-COMPARE-2025-REV2026](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/feds/linear-and-nonlinear-econometric-models-against-machine-learning-models.htm); [D011-JEF-REALIZED-VOL-ML-2024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jempfin.2024.101524) **Limit:** The Fed FEDS paper is preliminary author research and the peer-reviewed 2024 study covers ten equity indices and a bounded sample. Compare on task-specific rolling out-of-sample designs and guard against leakage; no model family is universally superior.
- **Risk-neutral derivative valuation differs from real-world return forecasting** Ã¢â‚¬â€ No-arbitrage replication/pricing values an option under a pricing measure implied by replicating portfolios or risk-neutral probabilities; it does not require predicting the underlying's actual expected return or real-world up/down probabilities. Discrete-time binomial models make hedge ratios and early-exercise decisions visible; continuous-time BSM/Black formulas are analytic models under stronger assumptions. Black is used for specified futures/rate options and swaptions. These are related pricing formulations whose fit depends on payoff, instrument and assumptions, not a sequence of statistical forecasts. **Sources:** [D011-CFA-CONTINGENT-CLAIMS-MODELS-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/valuation-contingent-claims); [D011-CFA-CONTINGENT-CLAIMS-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/valuation-contingent-claims); [D011-CFA-DERIVATIVES-2026-PDF](https://www.cfainstitute.org/sites/default/files/docs/programs/cfa-program/2026-l2-topics-combined.pdf); [D011-ONET-QFA-2026](https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/13-2099.01) **Limit:** The CFA pages provide curriculum-level models and applications; they do not cover every payoff or model assumption. Do not confuse a risk-neutral pricing measure with a student's statistical forecast or physical probability estimate.
- **Analytic formulas, trees, finite differences and Monte Carlo are pricing engines, not competing financial products** Ã¢â‚¬â€ The same contract can be priced using different calculation engines when model assumptions permit: closed-form Black/BSM for supported European structures, tree/lattice backward induction for discrete-time and exercise decisions, finite-difference grids for pricing PDEs, and Monte Carlo/pathwise simulation for path-dependent or high-dimensional payoffs. The relevant choice depends on payoff/exercise features, model, convergence/error controls and computational budget. A platform's listed engine availability is evidence of implementation, not proof an engine is accurate or best for every contract. **Sources:** [D011-QUANTLIB-OPTION-ENGINE-COMPARISON](https://github.com/lballabio/QuantLib/blob/master/Examples/EquityOption/EquityOption.cpp); [D011-OPEN-GAMMA-PRODUCT-COVERAGE](https://strata.opengamma.io/product_coverage/); [D011-CFA-CONTINGENT-CLAIMS-MODELS-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/valuation-contingent-claims); [D011-CFA-ARBITRAGE-FREE-FIXED-INCOME-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/arbitrage-free-valuation-framework) **Limit:** Engine coverage varies by product and software version. The code example demonstrates implementation comparison; method assumptions, convergence and product-specific numerical error need separate validation. Engine alternatives do not imply students must learn every engine in one path.
- **Yield-curve construction and calibration feed pricing, while model calibration and validation are separate** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Curve construction uses selected observable market instruments, conventions, discount/forward curve purposes, interpolation and a calibration measure/root finder. The calibrated curve becomes an input to pricing and curve-risk calculations. For embedded optionality or rate derivatives, a term-structure model can then be fit/used to represent rate dynamics, with a tree or Monte Carlo path valuation. Matching input instruments is curve calibration; it does not validate dynamics, extrapolation, hedging performance or model suitability. This is a technical data-to-model dependency in pricing work, not automatically a learner-level blocker edge. **Sources:** [D011-OPEN-GAMMA-RATES-CURVE-CALIBRATOR](https://strata.opengamma.io/apidocs/com/opengamma/strata/pricer/curve/RatesCurveCalibrator.html); [D011-OPEN-GAMMA-CURVE-CALIBRATION](https://strata.opengamma.io/curve_calibration_loader/); [D011-CFA-ARBITRAGE-FREE-FIXED-INCOME-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/arbitrage-free-valuation-framework); [D011-QUANTLIBPY-TERM-STRUCTURES-2026](https://quantlib-python-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/termstructures.html) **Limit:** Curve nodes, day-count/calendar conventions, interpolation and multi-curve framework depend on currency, collateral, instrument liquidity and market regime. Project documentation demonstrates implementation details, not a universal methodology or data-quality certification.
- **Fixed-income pricing branches by cash-flow optionality and rate dynamics** Ã¢â‚¬â€ A non-option bond can be valued from cash flows discounted on the relevant spot/discount curve. Embedded or standalone rate options require modeling future rate states or paths: calibrated binomial lattices support backward induction and early exercise; pathwise/Monte Carlo simulation handles simulated rate paths and other structures. Equilibrium and arbitrage-free approaches differ in how they represent and fit the current curve. Choice depends on contractual optionality, rate exposure, calibration instruments and output needs; one tree or short-rate model is not a universal fixed-income pricer. **Sources:** [D011-CFA-ARBITRAGE-FREE-FIXED-INCOME-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/arbitrage-free-valuation-framework); [D011-OPEN-GAMMA-PRODUCT-COVERAGE](https://strata.opengamma.io/product_coverage/); [D011-OPEN-GAMMA-RATES-CURVE-CALIBRATOR](https://strata.opengamma.io/apidocs/com/opengamma/strata/pricer/curve/RatesCurveCalibrator.html); [D011-BIS-MARKET-RISK-2026](https://www.bis.org/publications/fsi-summary-revised-market-risk-framework-executive-summary) **Limit:** CFA curriculum and platform coverage show method families, while BIS material covers banking exposure context; neither chooses a specific model for a given product. Rate model risk, negative-rate behavior, volatility surface, curve conventions and legal instrument terms need product-specific evidence.
- **Credit derivative valuation combines discounting and default-probability inputs** Ã¢â‚¬â€ A CDS/pricing workflow can infer a piecewise hazard/default-probability curve from quoted CDS spreads using a recovery assumption, contract conventions and a discount curve, then use survival/default probabilities and cash flows in valuation. This is distinct from a borrower credit score or a physical probability-of-default estimate: market-implied credit curves reflect market quotes and assumptions. The curve method connects derivative pricing with credit-risk modeling, but a single flat hazard rate is only a simplifying model. **Sources:** [D011-QUANTLIB-GUIDE-CREDIT-CURVES-2026](https://www.quantlibguide.com/Default-probability%20curves.html); [D011-QUANTLIBPY-TERM-STRUCTURES-2026](https://quantlib-python-docs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/termstructures.html); [D011-OPEN-GAMMA-PRODUCT-COVERAGE](https://strata.opengamma.io/product_coverage/); [D011-BIS-CREDIT-IRB](https://www.bis.org/committees/bcbs/basel-consolidated-guidelines/module/cri/30) **Limit:** The QuantLib guide is implementation instruction and the platform docs show available product families; neither establishes market-standard conventions on its own. Recovery, discounting, counterparty, liquidity, basis and ISDA documentation can materially alter the result; validate against current contract conventions.
- **Market-implied credit valuation and real-world default prediction answer different questions** Ã¢â‚¬â€ CVA/credit-derivative valuation uses market-implied default/survival information alongside discounted exposure and loss-given-default assumptions; a borrower's observed historical default likelihood is a different target. Regulatory material explicitly warns not to substitute risk-neutral default probabilities for observed default probabilities. This connects market spread/curve construction with derivative valuation and counterparty risk, while historical PD estimation remains a separate credit-risk task. **Sources:** [D011-BIS-CVA-CREDIT-VALUATION-FRAMEWORK](https://www.bis.org/committees/bcbs/basel-framework/standard/mar/50/inforce/2023-01-01/published/2020-07-08); [D011-BIS-CREDIT-SPREAD-STRUCTURAL-REDUCED-FORM-2004](https://www.bis.org/publ/work160.pdf); [D011-QUANTLIB-GUIDE-CREDIT-CURVES-2026](https://www.quantlibguide.com/Default-probability%20curves.html) **Limit:** The Basel passage applies to its prudential CVA framework and is subject to local adoption; the BIS paper is a dated study. Risk-neutral and physical probabilities must be identified by valuation purpose and calibration inputs, not inferred from the label alone.
- **Structural and reduced-form credit models encode different default mechanisms** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Structural models derive default from a firm's asset-value process crossing a default boundary, linking credit claims to option/firm-value models. Reduced-form or intensity models represent default as a random event with modeled arrival intensity and survival probabilities. Both can support bond/CDS valuation or risk analysis but require different inputs, calibration and output interpretation; neither is a universal replacement for the other. Their calibration errors and model-specification errors must be assessed separately. **Sources:** [D011-BIS-CREDIT-SPREAD-STRUCTURAL-REDUCED-FORM-2004](https://www.bis.org/publ/work160.pdf); [D011-BIS-CREDIT-MODEL-CALIBRATION-ERRORS](https://www.bis.org/publications/measuring-portfolio-credit-risk-modelling-versus-calibration-errors); [D011-BIS-CVA-CREDIT-VALUATION-FRAMEWORK](https://www.bis.org/committees/bcbs/basel-framework/standard/mar/50/inforce/2023-01-01/published/2020-07-08) **Limit:** The BIS working papers are older, bounded research and do not establish a current model winner. The CVA rule defines a regulatory output rather than endorsing one general structural or intensity model; compare against current research and task-specific validation needs.
- **Pricing-engine architecture explains alternatives without claiming accuracy** Ã¢â‚¬â€ An instrument definition can be kept separate from a replaceable calculation engine, allowing analytic, tree, finite-difference or Monte Carlo implementations to price the same contract when their assumptions and payoff handling fit. That is a software architecture relationship and a useful explanation of alternatives; choosing an engine still requires numerical-analysis evidence about convergence, error, stability and computational cost for the specific product. **Sources:** [D011-QUANTLIB-REPLACEABLE-PRICING-ENGINES-5](https://www.quantlib.org/quep/quep005.html); [D011-QUANTLIB-OPTION-ENGINE-COMPARISON](https://github.com/lballabio/QuantLib/blob/master/Examples/EquityOption/EquityOption.cpp); [D011-OPEN-GAMMA-PRODUCT-COVERAGE](https://strata.opengamma.io/product_coverage/) **Limit:** QuantLib's proposal and implementation examples are credible for describing that project's architecture and available examples only. They are grey project evidence, not a comparative accuracy benchmark, market-practice survey or learner prerequisite specification.
- **Portfolio allocation methods branch by investor objective, liability and constraints** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Mean-variance optimization is one asset-only allocation framework. Liability-relative/surplus optimization, goals-based allocation, factor allocation and risk budgeting address different objectives or risk definitions; constraints, rebalancing, taxes, liquidity, time horizon and implementation costs modify how a target portfolio is made investable. Portfolio construction therefore follows a stated objective, expected-return/risk inputs and constraints, and leads to implementation and performance evaluation; there is no single method sequence that fits every mandate. **Sources:** [D011-CFA-ASSET-ALLOCATION-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/principles-asset-allocation); [D011-CFA-REAL-WORLD-ALLOCATION-CONSTRAINTS-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/asset-allocation-with-real-world-constraints); [D011-CFA-ACTIVE-EQUITY-PORTFOLIO-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/active-equity-investing-portfolio-construction) **Limit:** Current CFA curriculum is a professional teaching source, not a universal job requirement or evidence that each alternative applies to every investor. The selected objective and constraints must come from the actual portfolio mandate and governance context.
- **MVO extensions address input sensitivity and implementation limits in different ways** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Traditional MVO depends on expected-return and covariance estimates and can produce concentrated, input-sensitive weights. BlackÃ¢â‚¬â€œLitterman combines an equilibrium prior with investor views; constraints and resampling can limit certain pathologies; robust formulations model uncertainty in estimates; shrinkage regularizes covariance inputs; risk parity changes the allocation objective; and CVaR/semi-variance objectives focus on downside loss rather than variance. These are alternative or complementary design choices, not a ladder of compulsory methods. Compare resulting weights, exposures, turnover, costs and mandate fit. **Sources:** [D011-CFA-ASSET-ALLOCATION-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/principles-asset-allocation); [D011-STANFORD-MARKOWITZ-PRACTICAL-OPTIMIZATION-2024](https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/papers/markowitz.html); [D011-PYPORTFOLIOOPT-OPTIMIZATION-METHODS](https://github.com/PyPortfolio/PyPortfolioOpt); [D011-CVXPY-PORTFOLIO-QUADRATIC-PROGRAM](https://www.cvxpy.org/examples/basic/quadratic_program.html) **Limit:** The CFA summary and Stanford paper identify documented limitations/extensions; PyPortfolioOpt lists software implementations rather than validating them. No alternative is universally stable or superior; empirically compare against the relevant benchmark, input uncertainty and constraints.
- **Covariance estimation branches from sample moments to shrinkage and structured factor risk models** Ã¢â‚¬â€ The sample covariance is the transparent baseline but can be noisy, ill-conditioned or non-invertible when the asset dimension is large relative to the observation window; error in its inverse can produce unstable optimized weights. Linear shrinkage pulls a sample estimate toward a structured target; nonlinear/quadratic eigenvalue shrinkage changes eigenvalues more selectively; factor covariance reduces the free parameters through observed or latent factors. These are alternative estimators for the covariance input, not separate allocation objectives. Choice depends on sample-to-asset ratio, dependence/regime assumptions, factor specification, mandate constraints and whether the goal is covariance accuracy or realized portfolio risk. **Sources:** [D011-LEDOIT-WOLF-SHRINKAGE-2004](https://www.ledoit.net/honey_abstract.htm); [D011-LEDOIT-WOLF-NONLINEAR-SHRINKAGE-2012](https://doi.org/10.1214/12-AOS989); [D011-LEDOIT-WOLF-QUADRATIC-SHRINKAGE-2022](https://doi.org/10.3150/20-BEJ1315); [D011-CONLON-COTTER-KYNIGAKIS-FACTOR-COVARIANCE-2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0377221725002127); [D011-CFA-ASSET-ALLOCATION-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/principles-asset-allocation) **Role/task context:** quantitative analyst (conditional_direct): Relevant when the assignment estimates portfolio covariance, optimizes asset weights, measures portfolio risk, or builds/tests the corresponding model; an instrument-pricing-only assignment may not need portfolio covariance methods. Sources: [D011-ONET-QFA-2026](https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/13-2099.01); quantitative researcher (conditional_direct): Relevant when research builds portfolio/risk forecasts or allocation strategies; cited research-employer tasks also include financial time series and model building, but not every project is covariance or portfolio optimization. Sources: [D011-JS-QUANT-RESEARCHER-2026](https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/position/8600948002/), [D011-TS-QUANT-RESEARCHER-ML-2025](https://careers.twosigma.com/careers/JobDetail/New-York-New-York-United-States-Quantitative-Researcher-Machine-Learning/12634); financial risk specialist (conditional_direct): Relevant for portfolio/market-risk estimation and model development or monitoring; select an estimator only where the actual exposure and risk model use covariance structure. Sources: [D011-ONET-13-2054.00](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/13-2054.00), [D011-BLACKROCK-RQA-CAREER-2026](https://careers.blackrock.com/students-and-graduates-functions-risk-quantitative-analysis); asset manager (conditional_downstream): Relevant when the manager owns or interprets portfolio allocation, risk budgeting, factor allocation or systematic construction; the occupational source does not say every manager personally estimates covariance. Sources: [D011-ONET-11-3031.03](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/11-3031.03); quantitative trader (conditional_downstream): Relevant if the trading mandate includes portfolio-level position sizing, covariance-aware risk limits or portfolio construction; employer evidence also covers strategy execution and risk, but does not make every trading strategy covariance-based. Sources: [D011-JS-QUANT-TRADER-2026](https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/position/8573523002/); quantitative developer (conditional_implementation): Relevant when implementing, testing or operating covariance estimation and portfolio-optimization systems; implementation work does not itself choose or validate the financial estimator. Sources: [D011-P72-QUANT-DEV-TRADING-RESEARCH-2026](https://careers.point72.com/CSJobDetail?jobCode=IVS-0014934&jobName=quantitative-developer-trading-research&locale=English&location=Warsaw%2C+PL&retURL=%2FCSCareerSearch); investment analyst (conditional_downstream): Relevant when analyst duties include portfolio analytics, investment-risk measurement or systematic allocation; general valuation and recommendation duties alone do not establish covariance estimation as required. One Ford Foundation investment-analytics posting documents such duties, but its deadline passed and its direct page was unreadable. Sources: [D011-ONET-13-2051.00](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/13-2051.00), [D011-FORD-INVESTMENT-ANALYTICS-ANALYST-2026](https://fordfoundation.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/FordFoundationCareerPage/job/Investment-Analytics-Analyst_R1303); statistician (conditional_method_transfer): Statistical estimation expertise transfers when assigned to a financial portfolio/risk problem; generic statistician tasks do not establish finance specialization or this technique as a role requirement. Sources: [D011-ONET-15-2041.00](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/15-2041.00) **Limit:** Sources establish method families and bounded results; no estimator is universally best. Covariance loss and portfolio loss are different evaluation targets, and nonstationarity, serial dependence, missing data, constraints, transaction costs and estimation windows can change rankings. Test with rolling or otherwise time-respecting out-of-sample evaluation.
- **ML can regularize, learn covariance structure or tune shrinkage inside portfolio construction** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Machine-learning links here are more specific than 'apply ML to finance': regularization and cross-validation can target portfolio-level estimation risk; PCA/PLS can construct lower-dimensional latent factors for covariance; reinforcement learning or supervised policy learning can tune shrinkage intensity; and recent work learns strategy/constraint-aware covariance structure. These methods extend the classical chain (returns Ã¢â€ â€™ covariance/risk estimate Ã¢â€ â€™ constrained portfolio weights Ã¢â€ â€™ cost-aware evaluation). They may be complementary to conventional estimators or alternative estimators, but they do not replace the portfolio objective, financial assumptions, comparators or validation. Compare against sample covariance, linear/nonlinear shrinkage, factor models, 1/N and relevant mandate baselines using chronological data splits, turnover/transaction costs and stability diagnostics. **Sources:** [D011-ELKAROUI-LIM-ML-PORTFOLIO-2018](https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mnsc.2016.2644); [D011-CONLON-COTTER-KYNIGAKIS-FACTOR-COVARIANCE-2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0377221725002127); [D011-GOLDBERG-GURDOGAN-KERCHEVAL-EIGENVECTOR-SHRINKAGE-2025](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00780-025-00566-4); [D011-MATTERA-RL-COVARIANCE-SHRINKAGE-2023](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2667305323000066); [D011-NEURAL-NONLINEAR-SHRINKAGE-2026](https://academic.oup.com/jfec/article/24/2/nbag002/8512976); [D011-QUANTCONNECT-PORTFOLIO-TO-EXECUTION-FLOW](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/algorithm-framework/overview) **Limit:** Recent ML comparisons are research proposals/results on bounded datasets, not evidence of universal or live-market superiority. The Linked QuantConnect documentation supports only the downstream software handoff, not the validity of a learned estimate. Treat any learned covariance/parameter policy as a model requiring leakage controls, independent evaluation and governance.
- **Systematic signals feed portfolio targets, risk controls and execution through distinct stages** Ã¢â‚¬â€ A systematic workflow can turn a universe and research signals/forecasts into target holdings, then apply portfolio risk constraints and send adjusted targets to execution. Portfolio construction is not the same as alpha research, risk management or execution: each stage consumes different inputs and yields a different artifact. Platform docs make this handoff explicit, while current portfolio-construction material shows that liquidity, turnover, market impact and mandate limits feed back into feasible weights and execution choices. **Sources:** [D011-QUANTCONNECT-PORTFOLIO-TO-EXECUTION-FLOW](https://www.quantconnect.com/docs/v2/writing-algorithms/algorithm-framework/overview); [D011-CFA-ACTIVE-EQUITY-PORTFOLIO-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/active-equity-investing-portfolio-construction); [D011-MSCI-PORTFOLIO-CONSTRUCTION-2026](https://www.msci.com/research-and-insights/paper/the-common-language-of-portfolio-construction); [D011-FINRA-ALGORITHMIC-STRATEGY-CONTROLS](https://www.finra.org/sites/default/files/notice_doc_file_ref/Notice_Regulatory_15-09.pdf) **Limit:** QuantConnect documents its own software architecture and MSCI's 2026 source was only publicly previewed; CFA curriculum and FINRA controls have distinct scopes. The stage model is useful context, not proof of one universal architecture, canonical graph edge or method prerequisite.
- **Trade-cost measurement, execution schedules, order choice and learned execution policies are connected but distinct** Ã¢â‚¬â€ For a desired position or alpha signal, the learner must distinguish (a) measuring completed-trade cost from choosing an execution policy, (b) static schedules/benchmarks such as TWAP or VWAP from adaptive policies, and (c) a price-impact model from the optimizer that uses it. Implementation shortfall captures explicit cost, impact, delay and unfilled opportunity cost more fully than VWAP cost estimates, while neither benchmark is itself automatically an algorithm. Classical BertsimasÃ¢â‚¬â€œLo expected-cost control and AlmgrenÃ¢â‚¬â€œChriss cost/volatility optimization provide tractable baselines; market-versus-limit order models add fill probability, order-book depth and completion risk; FX practice sources describe passive, sweeping, participation and hybrid choices under different urgency/liquidity trade-offs. Supervised cost/fill prediction or RL can then estimate uncertain components or learn state-dependent actions. Recent RL papers explicitly build on classical objectives/models and report generalization, calibration, out-of-distribution and model-misspecification limits. Thus ML is a possible downstream extension of execution modeling/control, not a replacement for understanding costs, market microstructure, baseline schedules, constraints and chronological/out-of-sample evaluation. **Sources:** [D011-CFA-TCA-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/trading-costs-and-electronic-markets); [D011-BIS-FX-EXECUTION-ALGORITHMS-2020](https://www.bis.org/publications/fx-execution-algorithms-and-market-functioning); [D011-BERTIMAS-LO-EXECUTION-1998](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1386418197000128); [D011-ALMGREN-CHRISS-EXECUTION-2001](https://doi.org/10.21314/JOR.2001.041); [D011-CARTEA-JAIMUNGAL-EXECUTION-ORDERS-2015](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/14697688.2015.1032543); [D011-IJCAI-GENERALIZABLE-RL-EXECUTION-2023](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2023/553); [D011-CHEN-LUDOVSKI-VOSS-ML-EXECUTION-SURROGATES-2023](https://doi.org/10.1080/14697688.2023.2282657); [D011-WANG-GAO-LI-RL-EXECUTION-2026](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00780-026-00589-5) **Role/task context:** quantitative trader (conditional task connection): Only where the role assignment includes translating signals or target positions into orders, optimizing fills/costs, or evaluating execution; alpha research alone does not establish execution ownership. Sources: [D011-JS-QUANT-TRADER-2026](https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/position/8573523002/) **Limit:** Sources range from professional curriculum and a 2020 FX institutional report to bounded research models/simulators. They establish task/method distinctions and candidate relationships, not a universal sequence, a claim that every quantitative trader implements these methods, or proof any current algorithm outperforms in live trading. The relevant quant-trader role evidence is employer-specific and only supports routes where execution is an assigned task.
- **Financial econometric estimators and empirical designs branch by data structure and research question** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Regression and inference foundations support several different branches. OLS, robust/clustered inference, MLE and GMM are estimation/inference choices; MLE uses a specified likelihood while GMM uses moment restrictions, and the latter includes IV-GMM rather than serving as a separate causal design. With repeated firms/assets over time, pooled OLS, fixed effects, random effects, first differences and other panel estimators rely on different assumptions; Famaâ€“MacBeth is a two-pass cross-sectional asset-pricing procedure, not a generic substitute for panel regression. For endogeneity, IV/2SLS, LIML and IV-GMM require relevant, defensible instruments and diagnostic checks. DiD, RDD, randomized designs and selection-on-observables address causal questions under different identification assumptions. A finance event study estimates normal return and abnormal market response around an event using estimation/event windows and tests; it is a design for market reactions, not automatically a causal experiment. Select based on estimand, assignment/data structure, identifying assumptions, dependence, horizon and inferenceâ€”not by method popularity. These branches can combine when a concrete design calls for it, but each connection is conditional rather than a universal sequence. **Sources:** [D011-BIRMINGHAM-FINANCIAL-ECONOMETRICS-2026](https://program-and-modules-handbook.bham.ac.uk/webhandbooks/WebHandbooks-control-servlet?Action=getModuleDetailsList&pgCrse=36331&pgSubj=07&searchTerm=002026); [D011-YORK-FINANCIAL-ECONOMETRICS-2026](https://www.york.ac.uk/students/studying/manage/programmes/module-catalogue/module/ECO00084M/2026-27?creditLevel=&department=&electiveTheme=&isAvailableAsElective=false&isAvailableToVisitingStudents=true&max=15&offset=180&query=&teachingPeriod=); [D011-NHH-FINANCIAL-ECONOMETRICS-2026](https://www.nhh.no/en/courses/financial-econometrics2/); [D011-LINEARMODELS-7-1](https://bashtage.github.io/linearmodels/); [D011-FAMA-MACBETH-1973](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/260061); [D011-ELGHOUL-INTERNATIONAL-EVENT-STUDY-2022](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35822194/) **Role/task context:** quantitative analyst (conditional research task connection): Use these designs only when the assigned work studies financial data with a cross-sectional, panel, event-response, asset-pricing or causal estimand; a role title alone does not show that every design is used. Sources: [D011-ONET-QFA-2026](https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/13-2099.01); quantitative researcher (conditional research task connection): Relevant when the research assignment is empirical finance/asset-pricing or estimates a causal/structural parameter; the cited posting supports quantitative model/statistical research generally, not each named design individually. Sources: [D011-JS-QUANT-RESEARCHER-2026](https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/position/8600948002/) **Limit:** The curricula show representative finance-method coverage and implementation docs enumerate estimator families; neither curriculum inclusion nor package availability determines a method's validity for a specific dataset. Identification and inference assumptions, market structure and design-specific diagnostics remain decisive. This note is evidence for route review, not an approved graph edge or compulsory course sequence.
- **Machine learning can extend finance prediction and econometric nuisance estimation, but ordinary prediction does not identify causality** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Finance ML research applies regularized regression, trees and neural nets to high-dimensional asset-pricing predictors and tests whether flexible interactions improve out-of-sample prediction against regression benchmarks. This is predictive modeling and needs time-aware evaluation; it does not by itself identify why a predictor affects returns. For causal/structural inference, double/debiased ML uses flexible learners for high-dimensional nuisance functions inside Neyman-orthogonal estimating equations with cross-fitting, while the target parameter and identification assumptions remain econometric. These are different ways to combine modern ML with traditional methods: predictive ML extends the forecast model, whereas DML extends estimation of nuisance components while preserving a design-based estimand and inference. Neither method repairs an invalid instrument, weak overlap, unmodeled dependence or a misspecified causal design. **Sources:** [D011-RFS-ML-ASSET-PRICING-2020](https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhaa009); [D011-CHERNOZHUKOV-DML-2018](https://academic.oup.com/ectj/article/21/1/C1/5056401?login=false); [D011-SCIKIT-TIME-SERIES-SPLIT](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/cross_validation.html) **Role/task context:** quantitative researcher (conditional research task connection): Prediction methods apply where research produces return/risk forecasts; DML applies only when the research question has an identified low-dimensional causal/structural target and valid data design. Sources: [D011-JS-QUANT-RESEARCHER-2026](https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/position/8600948002/); quantitative analyst (conditional model-development connection): Use only for assigned predictive or inferential model-development tasks; the broad occupational model-development evidence does not imply that every analyst uses ML or DML. Sources: [D011-ONET-QFA-2026](https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/13-2099.01) **Limit:** Asset-pricing results are bounded to the paper's US equity data/predictors and out-of-sample protocol. DML guarantees depend on stated orthogonality, identification, convergence and dependence conditions; an ML model's predictive accuracy is not evidence of causal identification. These links are research-context candidates, not route prerequisites.
- **Strategy-selection methods, execution governance and client-facing FX disclosure form separate but connected layers** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Multiple-testing and backtest-overfit diagnostics assess evidence after researchers explore candidate strategies; they do not constrain live order submission or prove operational controls. Algorithmic-trading rules and supervisory guidance (EU MiFID II Article 17/ESMA 2026 briefing; U.S. SEC Rule 15c3-5/FINRA guidance) address firm governance, testing, pre-trade limits, access and monitoring in their own legal perimeters. In FX client execution, the CBN FX Code explainer and GFXC templates focus on disclosure, provider due diligence and transaction-cost-analysis data. A real workflow may use strategy research and selection diagnostics before controlled deployment, then monitor order/risk controls and disclose client execution service characteristics; the sequence is an explanatory lifecycle, not a universal legal path. TCA can feed execution evaluation but is not the same as a return-predictive backtest or a multiple-testing adjustment. **Sources:** [D011-WHITE-REALITY-CHECK-2000](https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-0262.00152); [D011-HANSEN-SPA-2005](https://doi.org/10.1198/073500105000000063); [D011-PBO-BACKTEST-OVERFIT-2017](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/4w1110bb); [D011-ESMA-MIFID-II-ARTICLE-17-ALGO-TRADING](https://www.esma.europa.eu/publications-and-data/interactive-single-rulebook/mifid-ii/article-17-algorithmic-trading); [D011-ESMA-ALGO-TRADING-SUPERVISORY-BRIEFING-2026](https://www.esma.europa.eu/document/supervisory-briefing-algorithmic-trading-eu); [D011-SEC-RULE-15C3-5-FINAL-2011](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/2011/06/risk-management-controls-brokers-or-dealers-market-access); [D011-SEC-MARKET-ACCESS-FAQ-STAFF](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/staff-guidance/trading-markets-frequently-asked-questions/divisionsmarketregfaq-0); [D011-FINRA-ALGO-STRATEGY-CONTROLS-2015](https://www.finra.org/sites/default/files/notice_doc_file_ref/Notice_Regulatory_15-09.pdf); [D011-CBN-NIGERIAN-FX-CODE-PRIMARY-2025](https://www.cbn.gov.ng/Out/2025/CCD/Nigeria%20FX%20Code%20.pdf); [D011-CBN-NIGERIAN-FX-CODE-LAUNCH-2025](https://www.cbn.gov.ng/FeaturedArticles/2025/FX_Code_Launch.html); [D011-CBN-NIGERIAN-FX-CODE-ALGO-DISCLOSURE-2025](https://www.cbn.gov.ng/Out/2025/CCD/CBN%20UPDATE%20APRIL%202025.pdf); [D011-GFXC-ALGO-TCA-TEMPLATES](https://www.globalfxc.org/the-importance-of-disclosures-and-transparency-in-the-fx-market/algo-tca-templates/) **Limit:** EU and U.S. legal sources have defined institutional and jurisdictional scope; FINRA is member-firm guidance, ESMA's 2026 briefing is nonbinding, and the CBN newsletter is an explainer rather than the primary code. GFXC templates are voluntary. These sources support contextual learning and relationship mapping, not automatic legal applicability, a universal student prerequisite or a canonical graph edge.
- **High-frequency volatility measurement and volatility forecasting are two linked but different method choices** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Begin by distinguishing the target: latent integrated variance, the observed realized-variation measure, conditional variance from daily return history, option-implied future volatility, or a forecast of a realized-volatility series. For high-frequency prices, raw realized variance can be contaminated by market microstructure noise at very fine sampling; two-scale/subsampling and realized-kernel methods address noise under their respective assumptions. Bipower variation can help separate continuous variance from jump variation when its conditions hold, but does not itself remove arbitrary microstructure noise. After constructing a defensible measure, a separate forecast branch may use GARCH/SV on return histories, HAR/AR/VAR-style models on realized measures, or ML/DL extensions. These can be complements in a design pipeline (for example, noise-aware intraday measurement -> HAR-RV forecast -> VaR/ES calibration or volatility input), not a compulsory sequence containing every estimator and model. Recent comparisons do not show an invariant ML advantage: the answer changes with horizon, predictor set, forecast loss and economic decision value. **Sources:** [D011-ZHANG-MYKLAND-AITSAHALIA-TWO-SCALE-RV-2005](https://swh.princeton.edu/~yacine/twoscales.pdf); [D011-BARNDORFF-HANSEN-LUNDE-SHEPHARD-REALIZED-KERNEL-2008](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3982/ECTA6495); [D011-BARNDORFF-SHEPHARD-BIPOWER-JUMPS-2004](https://public.econ.duke.edu/~get/browse/courses/883/Spr16/COURSE-MATERIALS/Z_Papers/BNSJFEC2004.pdf); [D011-NBER-REALIZED-VOL-2001](https://www.nber.org/papers/w8160); [D011-CORSI-HAR-RV-2009](https://doi.org/10.1093/jjfinec/nbp001); [D011-ARCH-VOLATILITY-PROCESSES-2026](https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/stable/univariate/volatility.html); [D011-JEF-REALIZED-VOL-ML-2024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jempfin.2024.101524); [D011-FED-REALIZED-VOL-ML-COMPARE-2025-REV2026](https://www.federalreserve.gov/econres/feds/linear-and-nonlinear-econometric-models-against-machine-learning-models.htm); [D011-LEUSHUIS-PETKOV-REALIZED-VOL-FORECASTING-REVIEW-2026](https://doi.org/10.1186/s40854-025-00809-5) **Role/task context:** quantitative researcher (conditional empirical volatility modeling and method comparison): Relevant when the assignment develops or validates return/volatility models or high-frequency measures; a quant-research title alone does not imply this asset or method family. Sources: [D011-CITADEL-GQS-QUANT-RESEARCHER-2026](https://www.citadel.com/careers/details/global-quantitative-strategies-quantitative-researcher/); financial risk specialist (conditional volatility inputs for risk measurement and forecast validation): Relevant when volatility forecasts feed portfolio, market-risk or VaR/ES tasks; the source supports a role family, not an automatic requirement for realized-kernel estimation. Sources: [D011-BLACKROCK-RQA-CAREER-2026](https://careers.blackrock.com/students-and-graduates-functions-risk-quantitative-analysis); quantitative analyst (conditional pricing/risk model implementation and validation): Relevant when the quant assignment estimates or consumes volatility for an identified pricing or risk model; distinguish historical/realized measures from risk-neutral implied volatility. Sources: [D011-CITI-RATES-XVA-QUANT-ANALYST-2026](https://jobs.citi.com/job/london/quantitative-analyst-rates-xva-avp/287/100724661328); quantitative trader (conditional volatility forecast use in strategy or risk decisions): Relevant when the strategy uses volatility estimates or forecasts; realized-volatility prediction is not inherently a trading signal or universal trader task. Sources: [D011-JS-QUANT-TRADER-2026](https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/position/8573523002/) **Limit:** The source studies use different assets, sampling periods, noise/jump assumptions, targets, forecast horizons and evaluation criteria. A literature review covering through H1 2024 is not a 2026 exhaustive census. This note describes evidence-backed choices and combinations, not a universal estimator, method item requirement or graph edge.
- **Learned derivative-pricing approximators extend numerical pricing pipelines; they do not erase the structural model or validation problem** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Keep three layers distinct: a structural pricing model (for example Black–Scholes, local volatility or Heston), a numerical solver (analytic/semi-analytic formula, tree, finite difference, Monte Carlo or BSDE solver), and a learned surrogate/parameterization. Deep BSDE methods reformulate selected PDEs and approximate solution gradients to address high dimensionality; neural SDE/PDE methods can flexibly fit dynamics or pricing functions; learned surrogates can accelerate repeated evaluation after expensive simulation/calibration. These choices have different inputs and outputs and should be compared on the same payoff, market data, calibration window, out-of-sample prices/Greeks, stability and computational budget. Traditional methods remain benchmarks and may be complements that generate labels or validate a learned approximation. **Sources:** [D011-QUANTLIB-OPTION-ENGINE-COMPARISON](https://github.com/lballabio/QuantLib/blob/master/Examples/EquityOption/EquityOption.cpp); [D011-OPEN-GAMMA-PRODUCT-COVERAGE](https://strata.opengamma.io/product_coverage/); [D011-PNAS-DEEP-BSDE-PRICING-2018](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1718942115); [D011-FAN-SIRIGNANO-ML-PRICING-2026](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/14697688.2026.2623901); [D011-LUDKOVSKI-STAT-ML-QUANT-FINANCE-2023](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-statistics-032921-042409) **Role/task context:** quantitative analyst (conditional pricing-model development/validation task): Relevant where the analyst assignment explicitly implements, calibrates or validates derivative pricing models; not every quantitative analyst works on derivatives. Sources: [D011-CITI-FX-OPTIONS-QUANT-ANALYST-2026](https://jobs.citi.com/job/london/quantitative-analyst-fx-options-electronic-pricing-and-automation-vp/287/101394339872), [D011-CITI-EQUITY-DERIVATIVES-QUANT-2026](https://jobs.citi.com/job/london/front-office-equity-derivatives-quant-c-pricing-models-vp/287/102161054544); quantitative developer (conditional pricing-engine implementation task): Relevant where developer work implements or supports a derivatives pricing/risk platform; the listed employer example is one role-specific case. Sources: [D011-CITI-QUANT-TECH-DEVELOPER-2026](https://jobs.citi.com/job/pune/quantitative-technology-developer-python-and-c-vice-president/287/100400109312); quantitative researcher (conditional model research/comparison task): Relevant where the research assignment studies pricing dynamics, numerical accuracy, model calibration or learned approximations; title alone does not establish a specific model family. Sources: [D011-JS-QUANT-RESEARCHER-2026](https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/position/8600948002/) **Limit:** The papers study defined model classes, instruments, datasets and experiments; abstracts/reviews do not establish production performance or universal superiority. Strata and QuantLib document their own supported implementations, not field prevalence. This is a sourced comparison for later mapping review, not an approved item, graph edge or learning order.
- **Deep hedging is an objective-driven trading/control extension to derivative hedging, not a replacement pricing formula** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Classical model-based hedging derives sensitivities (such as Greeks) from a pricing model and usually begins with frictionless or simplified assumptions. Deep hedging instead represents trading decisions as a learned policy and optimizes a specified risk measure across market scenarios while explicitly allowing frictions such as transaction costs, liquidity constraints and market impact. A sensible design uses model-based hedge/pricing results as a benchmark, then evaluates the learned policy against a clear scenario generator, risk preference, constraints and out-of-sample performance. Its output is a hedge policy/strategy under the stated objective, not automatically a fair value for the derivative. **Sources:** [D011-BUEHLER-DEEP-HEDGING-2019](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.03042); [D011-CFA-CONTINGENT-CLAIMS-MODELS-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/valuation-contingent-claims); [D011-CFA-TRADE-STRATEGY-EXECUTION-2026](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/trade-strategy-execution) **Role/task context:** quantitative trader (conditional hedge/strategy task): Use when assigned to design, execute or evaluate derivative hedging under trading costs or inventory/risk constraints; this is not a universal trader method. Sources: [D011-JS-QUANT-TRADER-2026](https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/position/8573523002/); quantitative researcher (conditional policy/model research task): Use where research explicitly optimizes or evaluates hedging policies under frictions; generic ML research does not imply deep hedging use. Sources: [D011-JS-QUANT-RESEARCHER-2026](https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/position/8600948002/) **Limit:** The original paper's experiments do not establish superiority across products, markets, objectives or regimes; policy quality depends on the chosen scenario generator, risk measure, trading instruments and constraints. The relationship is explanatory evidence for later review, not a universal prerequisite or canonical graph edge.
- **Backtest/model-selection diagnostics answer different multiple-testing questions and should be chosen by output, not treated as interchangeable** Ã¢â‚¬â€ First freeze and disclose the searched candidate universe, benchmark, loss/return measure, time window and trial ledger. White's Reality Check asks whether the best candidate in the searched family beats a benchmark, using a dependence-aware bootstrap; Hansen's SPA refines this benchmark test with studentization and sample-dependent null recentering, reducing sensitivity to weak alternatives. Romano–Wolf StepM returns which candidates beat a benchmark while controlling familywise error. Hansen–Lunde–Nason MCS returns a set of candidates not statistically distinguished from the best under a chosen loss and needs no benchmark. DSR adjusts a selected Sharpe ratio for the number/effective number of trials and non-normality. PBO/CSCV instead estimates how often an in-sample winner ranks poorly out of sample under combinatorial splits. Harvey–Liu–Zhu's higher significance hurdle addresses cross-sectional factor discovery; it is not a direct replacement for a strategy-level test. These methods are complements only when the research question and assumptions warrant them, not a mandatory bundle. **Sources:** [D011-WHITE-REALITY-CHECK-2000](https://doi.org/10.1111/1468-0262.00152); [D011-HANSEN-SPA-2005](https://doi.org/10.1198/073500105000000063); [D011-ROMANO-WOLF-STEPM-2005](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1468-0262.2005.00615.x); [D011-HANSEN-LUNDE-NASON-MCS-2011](https://doi.org/10.3982/ECTA5771); [D011-BAILEY-LOPEZ-DSR-2014](https://www.davidhbailey.com/dhbpapers/deflated-sharpe.pdf); [D011-PBO-BACKTEST-OVERFIT-2017](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/4w1110bb); [D011-HARVEY-LIU-ZHU-FACTOR-MULTIPLE-TESTING-2016](https://doi.org/10.1093/rfs/hhv059); [D011-ARCH-MULTIPLE-COMPARISON-DOCS](https://arch.readthedocs.io/en/stable/multiple-comparison/multiple-comparison-reference.html) **Role/task context:** quantitative researcher (conditional strategy/model-selection research task): Use when the assignment searches and selects among many predictors, factors or strategies; direct research-task cards support research practice but not every test individually. Sources: [D011-JS-QUANT-RESEARCHER-2026](https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/position/8600948002/), [D011-TS-QUANT-RESEARCHER-ML-2025](https://careers.twosigma.com/careers/JobDetail/New-York-New-York-United-States-Quantitative-Researcher-Machine-Learning/12634); quantitative trader (conditional systematic-strategy validation task): Use when a trading assignment develops or selects signals/parameters through repeated historical backtests; it does not imply all trading roles conduct research or use every diagnostic. Sources: [D011-JS-QUANT-TRADER-2026](https://www.janestreet.com/join-jane-street/position/8573523002/); quantitative analyst (conditional predictive/model validation task): Use when tasked with validating forecasts or models selected from multiple candidates; this is not inferred from title alone. Sources: [D011-ONET-QFA-2026](https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/13-2099.01) **Limit:** The primary procedures target different hypotheses, statistics, candidate universes and outputs; source abstracts and library docs do not prove one method universally dominates. The methods are candidates for systematic-investment research and require exact assumptions/implementation review; no technique becomes a canonical learning item or dependency solely from this note.
- **Risk rules, regulatory capital measures and professional curricula answer different questions** Ã¢â‚¬â€ Basel MAR33 expected shortfall is a specific market-risk capital rule for banks using the internal models approach; CBN ICAAP/SREP guidance asks Nigerian banks to identify all material risks, quantify where suitable, assess internal capital and validate/stress-test the broader framework. Those are not interchangeable with a general practitioner’s VaR/ES estimate or a market-risk forecast. US Federal Reserve SR 26-2 is current model-risk guidance for its supervised-bank context, while SEC Nigeria adviser rules address client risk profiling, suitability and IPS records rather than institutional model risk. GARP FRM and CFA curricula organize learning coverage; they are credential syllabi, not statutes and not universal role prerequisites. The right contextual source depends on the employer, instrument, jurisdiction, portfolio/task and regulatory perimeter. A student-facing path should label these as conditional context choices and connect actual outputs (regulatory capital, internal capital/stress reports, model-validation evidence, or client suitability record) to the role task that consumes them. **Sources:** [D011-BIS-MAR33-EXPECTED-SHORTFALL-2026](https://www.bis.org/baselframework/BaselFramework.pdf); [D011-CBN-ICAAP-SRP-2021](https://www.cbn.gov.ng/Out/2021/BSD/7.%20REVISED%20GUIDELINES%20ON%20SUPERVISORY%20REVIEW%20PROCESS%20OF%20ICAAP.pdf); [D011-CBN-BASEL-II-III-NIGERIA](https://www.cbn.gov.ng/out/2020/fmd/cbn%20rule%20book%20volume%201.pdf); [D011-FED-SR26-2-2026](https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm); [D011-SEC-NIGERIA-ROBO-ADVISORY-RULES](https://home.sec.gov.ng/documents/1292/Rules-on-Robo-Advisory-Services_Executed-30-August-2021.pdf); [D011-GARP-FRM-CURRICULUM-2026](https://www.garp.org/frm/study-materials); [D011-CFA-2026-MEASURING-MANAGING-MARKET-RISK](https://www.cfainstitute.org/insights/professional-learning/refresher-readings/2026/measuring-managing-market-risk) **Limit:** Basel is implemented through local law; the CBN guideline and 2020 Nigerian capital framework need current-status confirmation; SR 26-2 has a U.S. supervisory scope; SEC adviser rules are client-advisory context. FRM/CFA syllabi show published learning scope, not hiring or licensing requirements. No universal curriculum order is inferred.
- **Initial-margin modelling consumes portfolio risk sensitivities, but it is not derivative pricing or market-risk capital** Ã¢â‚¬â€ ISDA SIMM v2.7+2412 uses sensitivities classified into risk-factor classes and aggregates delta, vega, curvature and other specified risk components to estimate initial margin for relevant non-centrally cleared derivatives. Under EU EMIR, firms may use the standardised grid or an authorised model; EBA centrally validates general aspects of the pro forma model while competent authorities authorize entity use and assess firm implementation. This is a downstream risk/collateral calculation, distinct from calculating a derivative's fair value or Basel market-risk capital. SIMM's currentness and regulatory context therefore belongs as a conditional risk-method/standards choice after derivative and portfolio risk foundations, not a universal prerequisite. Role evidence supports only broader conditional links: financial risk specialists may estimate/monitor risk and critique model outputs, while a derivatives quant analyst may build pricing and risk models. Those employer/occupational sources do not name SIMM; map the method to a role only when the assigned task actually covers uncleared-derivative margin, model implementation or validation. **Sources:** [D011-ISDA-SIMM-METHODOLOGY-V2-7-2025](https://www.isda.org/a/DRfgE/ISDA-SIMM_v2.72412_PUBLIC.pdf); [D011-EBA-CENTRAL-VALIDATION-ISDA-SIMM-2026](https://www.eba.europa.eu/activities/direct-supervision-and-oversight/validation-pro-forma-initial-margin-models); [D011-BIS-UNCLEARED-MARGIN-REVIEW-2025](https://www.bis.org/bcbs/publ/d606.pdf); [D011-BIS-MAR33-EXPECTED-SHORTFALL-2026](https://www.bis.org/baselframework/BaselFramework.pdf) **Role/task context:** financial risk specialist (conditional portfolio risk-model monitoring/validation context): Relevant only when the assigned portfolio includes in-scope uncleared derivatives and the specialist's task includes margin model risk, monitoring or review. The cited evidence supports broader risk estimation, stress testing and model-output critique; it does not state that this role uses SIMM specifically. Sources: [D011-BLACKROCK-RQA-CAREER-2026](https://careers.blackrock.com/students-and-graduates-functions-risk-quantitative-analysis); quantitative analyst (conditional derivatives risk-model implementation context): Relevant when the analyst develops or validates derivatives pricing/risk models and the specific product workflow includes regulatory initial margin. The cited Citi role supports derivatives pricing/risk model development but does not name SIMM or establish universal use. Sources: [D011-CITI-RATES-XVA-QUANT-ANALYST-2026](https://jobs.citi.com/job/london/quantitative-analyst-rates-xva-avp/287/100724661328) **Limit:** The detailed algorithm is proprietary/licensed and the public methodology is not independent validation. EBA statements are EU-specific, and entity/product thresholds must be checked in current law. BIS/BCBS corroborates implementation context, not global applicability. No role is asserted to use SIMM without task-specific evidence; this note supports later mapping review, not a graph edge or fixed learning dependency.
- **Market-risk estimates branch by portfolio and loss-distribution assumptions; regulatory backtesting is a separate validation layer** Ã¢â‚¬â€ For market-risk VaR estimation, U.S. banking regulation explicitly recognizes variance-covariance, historical-simulation and Monte Carlo approaches; they are alternative estimation engines whose assumptions, nonlinear position treatment, risk-factor coverage, data window and computational cost must be checked against the portfolio. EVT, filtered historical simulation and conditional autoregressive VaR are further research families, but the reviews found in this pass were not fully accessible, so these remain leads for primary-paper confirmation rather than settled comparative recommendations. Regulatory output is a separate choice: the current Basel internal-model framework calculates market-risk capital with expected shortfall while MAR32 uses VaR backtesting and P&L attribution tests as eligibility/validation components. Neither a method's permitted use nor a backtest alone establishes adequate model quality. Validation also has a distinct lifecycle: conceptual soundness, alternative assumptions/benchmarking, out-of-sample/out-of-time tests, outcome analysis, ongoing monitoring and stress testing scaled to model materiality. Thus the path should distinguish risk-measure estimation, regulatory capital calculation and model validation, and connect only the branch required by the learner's institution, portfolio and assignment. **Sources:** [D011-US-CFR-2026-217-203-MARKET-RISK-APPROACHES](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2026-title12-vol2/pdf/CFR-2026-title12-vol2-part217.pdf); [D011-BIS-MAR32-BACKTESTING-PLA-CURRENT](https://www.bis.org/committees/bcbs/basel-framework/standard/mar/32/inforce/2023-01-01/published/2020-03-27); [D011-BIS-MAR33-EXPECTED-SHORTFALL-2026](https://www.bis.org/baselframework/BaselFramework.pdf); [D011-FED-SR26-2-2026](https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisionreg/srletters/SR2602.htm); [D011-RISK-VAR-METHODOLOGY-REVIEW-2013](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.srfe.2013.06.001); [D011-DYNAMIC-EVT-VAR-ES-REVIEW-2024](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jempfin.2024.101488) **Role/task context:** financial risk specialist (conditional market-risk measurement and model monitoring): The role evidence supports statistical risk quantification, scenario analysis, risk-model development/monitoring and critique of model outputs. Specific estimator and bank regulatory capital tasks depend on the employer and portfolio; the cited evidence does not establish use of all three model families. Sources: [D011-ONET-13-2054.00](https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/13-2054.00), [D011-BLACKROCK-RQA-CAREER-2026](https://careers.blackrock.com/students-and-graduates-functions-risk-quantitative-analysis); quantitative analyst (conditional market-risk model development/validation): Relevant when a quantitative analyst's assignment builds or validates financial risk models; derivative-pricing roles may instead supply valuation/sensitivity inputs. The cited role examples are employer-specific and do not prove a universal VaR or Basel-capital task. Sources: [D011-ONET-QFA-2026](https://www.onetonline.org/link/details/13-2099.01), [D011-CITI-RATES-XVA-QUANT-ANALYST-2026](https://jobs.citi.com/job/london/quantitative-analyst-rates-xva-avp/287/100724661328) **Limit:** The CFR source applies to specified U.S. Board-regulated institutions under its market-risk rule; Basel standards depend on local adoption. The reviewed VaR papers differ in datasets, periods and evaluation, and their full texts were inaccessible in this search; no superiority ranking for EVT, FHS, CAViaR or any estimator is asserted. Broad role evidence does not show that a given role uses any named estimator or regulatory method.
- **Derivative-pricing numerical methods form conditional branches; Monte Carlo, QMC, variance reduction and machine learning play different roles** Ã¢â‚¬â€ A learner should first specify the contract/payoff, model dynamics, market inputs and target output, then choose a numerical approach whose assumptions fit. Analytic/transform methods (including Carr-Madan FFT or COS) use characteristic-function structure and are natural for some European claims; trees and PDE discretizations expose time/space and early-exercise structure on tractable dimensions; simulation estimates expectations and can handle selected path-dependent or multifactor contracts. Longstaff-Schwartz is an optimal-stopping regression method that estimates continuation values, with weighted least squares proposed for heteroscedastic regressions in tested settings. MC variance-reduction methods (antithetic, control variates, stratification/importance sampling), low-discrepancy QMC and MLMC modify estimator variance/cost or path allocation; they do not change the economic pricing model. Brownian bridge and PCA are path-construction choices whose benefits depend on payoff and effective dimension; discontinuity-alignment can improve some QMC/Greek problems, but counterexamples rule out a universal ranking. Neural control variates are a research extension layered over an expectation estimator, not a beginner prerequisite or replacement for classical controls. Finally, price, Greeks, numerical uncertainty, convergence and exercise-policy outputs need separate validation because accurate prices can coexist with inaccurate sensitivities. **Sources:** [D011-UCHICAGO-BLACK-SCHOLES-1973](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/pdf/10.1086/260062); [D011-ELSEVIER-CRR-1979](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/0304405X79900151); [D011-CUP-HULL-WHITE-EXPLICIT-FD-1990](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-financial-and-quantitative-analysis/article/abs/valuing-derivative-securities-using-the-explicit-finite-difference-method/3851DEE3A5EE3731D53EAA06A3D9E495); [D011-OUP-LONGSTAFF-SCHWARTZ-LSM-2001](https://academic.oup.com/rfs/article-abstract/14/1/113/1587472?login=true); [D011-CARR-MADAN-FFT-1999](https://wwwf.imperial.ac.uk/~ajacquie/IC_Num_Methods/IC_Num_Methods_Docs/Literature/CarrMadan.pdf);
