## D166 high-definition mapping relationships

These source-backed comparisons describe technique distinctions, alternatives, complements and claim limits for later graph review. They are not canonical items, student-display approvals, or graph/sequence edges.

- **Semantic lane maps, point-cloud maps and simulation road formats carry different kinds of road knowledge** -- A point-cloud map stores measured 3D surface/geometry and can support scan matching or map-relative perception; a vector/semantic lane map stores road/lane boundaries, topology, directions, traffic controls and participant-specific rules used for routing and behavior; some systems pair both. Lanelet2 is an operational map framework with participant-aware routing and traffic-rule interpretation. Apollo has a separate protobuf lane model. ASAM OpenDRIVE describes a static road network primarily for simulation exchange; OpenCRG adds detailed road-surface profiles and OpenSCENARIO describes dynamic actors/maneuvers that reference the static road network. These formats overlap in road representation but are not interchangeable substitutes: decide from consumer, required geometry/semantics, coordinate system, topology, update mechanism and conversion needs. A file extension or standard label alone does not prove the map has correct, fresh or complete content. **Sources:** [D166-AUTOWARE-MAP-INTERFACE-2026](https://docs.autoware.org/main/design/autoware-architecture-v1/interfaces/components/map/); [D166-AUTOWARE-MAP-CREATION-TUTORIAL-2026](https://docs.autoware.org/main/tutorials/integrating-autoware/creating-maps/); [D166-LANELET2-MAP-FRAMEWORK-PRIMARY](https://fzi-forschungszentrum-informatik.github.io/Lanelet2/); [D166-APOLLO-MAP-LANE-SCHEMA](https://github.com/ApolloAuto/apollo/blob/master/modules/common_msgs/map_msgs/map_lane.proto); [D166-ASAM-OPENDRIVE-2026](https://www.asam.net/standards/detail/opendrive/); [D166-ASAM-OPENCRG-ROAD-SURFACE](https://www.asam.net/standards/detail/opencrg/); [D166-ASAM-OPENSCENARIO-STATIC-DYNAMIC-CONTENT](https://www.asam.net/fileadmin/Standards/OpenSCENARIO/QUICK_READ_ASAM_OpenSCENARIO_BS-1-2_User-Guide_V1-0-0.html) **Role/task context:** software developer (conditional map data-model/interface task): Zoox, GM and map-infrastructure employer examples describe data formats, geometry/topology and downstream interfaces; apply when a developer owns the map schema or consumer contract. Sources: [D166-ZOOX-MAPPING-DATA-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://jobs.lever.co/zoox/8102c816-7ce1-49c8-8093-f46c8074652c), [D166-GM-SENIOR-SOFTWARE-MAPPING-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://generalmotors.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/Careers_GM/job/Senior-Machine-Learning-Engineer---Mapping_JR-202620459-1), [D166-APPLIED-MAPS-INFRASTRUCTURE-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/applied/366ad3c0-3988-4a94-a825-8fe6238a2a9a/) **Limit:** These sources document specific formats/implementations. OpenDRIVE is simulation-oriented; Lanelet2 and Apollo schema details are implementation-specific, and conversion may lose/alter semantics. Do not present any one schema as the universal AV map standard.
- **Map creation combines surveying or SLAM acquisition with georeferencing, feature extraction, semantics, topology and quality checks** -- A defensible map-production workflow begins with a use case, ODD, coordinate reference and required accuracy/semantic detail; acquires data through mobile mapping/survey, vehicle sensors or other surveyed sources; uses calibrated pose and sensor data to align observations; reconstructs geometry and extracts/annotates lanes, boundaries, signs, signals, crossings and other required features; attaches traffic/legal semantics and connects topological relations; converts into the chosen consumer schema; and validates geometric accuracy, semantic consistency, connectivity and downstream behavior before publishing a version. Manual editing, mobile-mapping surveys, SLAM-based point-cloud reconstruction and automated camera/LiDAR/ML extraction are context-dependent approaches that can be combined. A quick single-lane map from recorded pose is a prototype route, not a substitute for a complete production map. **Sources:** [D166-AUTOWARE-MAP-CREATION-TUTORIAL-2026](https://docs.autoware.org/main/tutorials/integrating-autoware/creating-maps/); [D166-TSUSHIMA-ETAL-HD-MAP-PRODUCTION-2020](https://isprs-archives.copernicus.org/articles/XLIII-B4-2020/415/2020/); [D166-LANELET2-MAP-VALIDATION](https://docs.ros.org/en/ros2_packages/humble/api/lanelet2_validation/__README.html); [D166-ASRAT-CHO-HD-MAP-SURVEY-2024](https://www.mdpi.com/2220-9964/13/7/232); [D166-HDMAP-TECHNOLOGY-REVIEW-2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2667325824000268); [D166-ARGOVERSE-HD-MAP-API](https://argoverse.github.io/user-guide/api/hd_maps.html) **Role/task context:** software developer (conditional map reconstruction, data pipeline or QA implementation): GM, NVIDIA and Applied Intuition examples describe distinct algorithm, infrastructure and map-authoring tasks; attach only the task branch actually assigned. Sources: [D166-GM-STAFF-ML-MAPPING-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://search-careers.gm.com/en/jobs/jr-202602984/staff-machine-learning-engineer-mapping/), [D166-NVIDIA-MAPPING-SOFTWARE-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://nvidia.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/NVIDIAExternalCareerSite/job/US-CA-Santa-Clara/Systems-Software-Engineer--Autonomous-Systems-Mapping---New-College-Graduate-2026_JR2020838), [D166-APPLIED-MAPPING-SPECIALIST-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/applied/cd80b2b9-d375-4050-b85e-ec6bb82a575c/), [D166-APPLIED-MAPS-INFRASTRUCTURE-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/applied/366ad3c0-3988-4a94-a825-8fe6238a2a9a/) **Limit:** Autoware and Lanelet2 provide practical examples; the production paper dates to 2020 and the two recent surveys are abstract/index-level here. The staged workflow synthesizes task families; do not treat it as a mandated single sequence or infer production accuracy without survey control, error budgets and acceptance criteria.
- **Map maintenance is a change-detection, evidence-fusion and controlled-release problem, not simply repeated map drawing** -- Road geometry and controls change, so fleets or survey teams can compare new sensor observations with a stored map, localize candidate discrepancies, aggregate corroborating observations, estimate confidence/quality, distinguish persistent infrastructure change from transient objects or construction, update affected geometry/semantics/topology, validate the changed region and dependent routes, version and release the update, and monitor its consumers. Crowdsourced fleet observations, remote sensing, vehicle camera/LiDAR/radar, human map editing and end-to-end learned lane/topology generation are possible data or automation sources under different latency, coverage, noise, privacy and trust assumptions. Research datasets can benchmark selected discrepancies; they do not establish a universal automatic-release policy. Map output needs provenance, temporal validity, quality gates and rollback/monitoring suitable to its use. **Sources:** [D166-ARGOVERSE-MAP-CHANGE-DATASET](https://argoverse.github.io/user-guide/datasets/map_change_detection.html); [D166-ARGOVERSE-HD-MAP-API](https://argoverse.github.io/user-guide/api/hd_maps.html); [D166-CROWD-MAP-QUALITY-2026](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1569843226002670); [D166-E2E-MAP-GENERATION-SURVEY-2026](https://jst.tsinghuajournals.com/EN/10.16511/j.cnki.qhdxxb.2026.28.018); [D166-ASRAT-CHO-HD-MAP-SURVEY-2024](https://www.mdpi.com/2220-9964/13/7/232); [D166-HDMAP-TECHNOLOGY-REVIEW-2025](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2667325824000268) **Role/task context:** software developer (conditional freshness/change-detection and map lifecycle task): GM, Waabi, PlusAI and Caterpillar postings describe map changes or create/validate/maintain systems; Caterpillar's listing is expired and mining-specific, and PlusAI combines mapping with localization. Sources: [D166-GM-STAFF-ML-MAPPING-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://search-careers.gm.com/en/jobs/jr-202602984/staff-machine-learning-engineer-mapping/), [D166-WAABI-MAPPING-SOFTWARE-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://jobs.lever.co/waabi/0e0ba69c-ea22-4bff-ac40-8e3e5674ff90), [D166-PLUSAI-MAPPING-LOCALIZATION-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://www.plus.ai/careers/527722d7-5887-4c96-9363-46eb3ea5cbc5/), [D166-CATERPILLAR-AUTONOMY-MAP-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://careers.caterpillar.com/en/jobs/r0000389353/autonomy-map-engineer/) **Limit:** The two 2026 papers and 2025 review are abstract/index-level in this pass; Argoverse is a bounded six-city dataset. Industry posting claims are company-specific. This note supports maintenance task context, not a validated autonomous update architecture or safe-release guarantee.
- **Map geometry, topology, semantics and version/freshness metadata serve localization, perception, routing/planning and simulation through different contracts** -- A map can be consumed as a geometric localization reference, a semantic prior for object or lane understanding, a participant-aware topology/traffic-rule graph for route and behavior planning, or a static road network for simulation. Consumers need compatible frames/projections, spatial resolution, element attributes, topology, map version/time and update interfaces. Autoware, Argoverse, Lanelet2 and Apollo expose different data contracts; OpenDRIVE can supply static simulation road-network content while OpenSCENARIO provides dynamic test actors. When a consumer finds an unavailable/stale/corrupt map or a data contract mismatch, its behavior must be considered separately from the map producer's quality check. The mapping area supports these consumers but does not own their localization, perception, planning or simulation algorithms. **Sources:** [D166-AUTOWARE-MAP-INTERFACE-2026](https://docs.autoware.org/main/design/autoware-architecture-v1/interfaces/components/map/); [D166-ARGOVERSE-HD-MAP-API](https://argoverse.github.io/user-guide/api/hd_maps.html); [D166-LANELET2-ROUTING-AND-RULES](https://github.com/fzi-forschungszentrum-informatik/Lanelet2/blob/master/lanelet2_routing/README.md); [D166-APOLLO-MAP-LANE-SCHEMA](https://github.com/ApolloAuto/apollo/blob/master/modules/common_msgs/map_msgs/map_lane.proto); [D166-ASAM-OPENDRIVE-2026](https://www.asam.net/standards/detail/opendrive/); [D166-ASAM-OPENSCENARIO-STATIC-DYNAMIC-CONTENT](https://www.asam.net/fileadmin/Standards/OpenSCENARIO/QUICK_READ_ASAM_OpenSCENARIO_BS-1-2_User-Guide_V1-0-0.html) **Role/task context:** software developer (conditional map-serving/data-consumer interface task): Zoox and Waabi examples cover developer/training/on-vehicle map interfaces; PlusAI covers map query and localization use. Apply only when the software assignment owns those interfaces. Sources: [D166-ZOOX-MAPPING-DATA-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://jobs.lever.co/zoox/8102c816-7ce1-49c8-8093-f46c8074652c), [D166-WAABI-MAPPING-SOFTWARE-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://jobs.lever.co/waabi/0e0ba69c-ea22-4bff-ac40-8e3e5674ff90), [D166-PLUSAI-MAPPING-LOCALIZATION-ROLE-2026-10-23](https://www.plus.ai/careers/527722d7-5887-4c96-9363-46eb3ea5cbc5/) **Limit:** These sources provide stack and dataset examples, not one shared interoperability contract. Mapping-source records document the data responsibility; they do not redefine ownership or sequencing for the consuming areas.
- **A prior high-definition map and an online vector-map estimate are different operating designs** -- ASAM OpenDRIVE 1.9.0 is explicitly a static road-network description used chiefly for simulation and exchange; its schema is not a complete live-map update system or the same thing as an operational lane-level map used by a vehicle stack. Lanelet2 encodes lanelets, traffic rules and routing graphs, with validators for geometry/topology/traffic-rule errors; the applicable participant and location affect route interpretation. Argoverse map-change data and crowdsourcing work treat map freshness and detecting changed road elements as a separate lifecycle problem. A 2025 online-temporal-fusion paper demonstrates a research branch that builds vectorized road maps from sequential sensor detections for mapless operation and a planning/control handoff. These routes can be alternatives under different map availability, update burden, ODD and system architecture; they can also coexist (e.g. prior map plus online change estimate) when an explicit design fuses them. Learner foundations include coordinate frames/georeferencing, road geometry and topology, lane semantics, quality/freshness, map validation and consumer interfaces. Outputs include versioned geometry/topology/attributes or change events, which localization consumes as map reference and planning consumes as lane/routing constraints. No paper establishes a universal mapless replacement or one canonical production data path. **Sources:** [D166-ASAM-OPENDRIVE-2026](https://www.asam.net/standards/detail/opendrive/); [D166-LANELET2-MAP-FRAMEWORK-PRIMARY](https://fzi-forschungszentrum-informatik.github.io/Lanelet2/); [D166-LANELET2-ROUTING-AND-RULES](https://github.com/fzi-forschungszentrum-informatik/Lanelet2/blob/master/lanelet2_routing/README.md); [D166-LANELET2-MAP-VALIDATION](https://docs.ros.org/en/ros2_packages/humble/api/lanelet2_validation/__README.html); [D166-ARGOVERSE-MAP-CHANGE-DATASET](https://argoverse.github.io/user-guide/datasets/map_change_detection.html); [D166-ONLINE-TEMPORAL-VECTORIZED-MAP-CONSTRUCTION-2025](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10897810/); [D166-TAICS-HD-MAP-STANDARDS-REGISTER-2025](https://en.hdmap.geomatics.ncku.edu.tw/article-published-documents.html) **Limit:** OpenDRIVE is a static simulation-road-network format; Lanelet2 is an open framework whose traffic rules are configured by region/participant; Argoverse map-change is a research dataset; the mapless-vector paper is abstract-level evidence. TAICS listing identifies regional standards only; original text was not inspected. These sources do not establish broad deployment or safety equivalence.

## Open learning, research and practitioner resources

These resources are indexed for discovery or instruction. They are kept separate from domain/area fit evidence and from evidence that a method or strategy is valid.

### D011

## D166 interface and integration relationships

### The vehicle interface translates between normalized ADS intent and platform-specific actuation/status contracts

Planning and control may describe target motion in normalized terms, while a particular drive-by-wire platform accepts its own steering, acceleration, brake, gear or other command representation. An interface adapter translates commands, normalizes returned status, exposes supported capabilities, and must account for feedback semantics and vehicle-specific calibration. This is an integration boundary: it connects control to hardware and returns state to localization/monitoring; it does not replace trajectory generation or controller design. Apollo's schema illustrates typed command identity and extensible operations, while Autoware documents command conversion and feedback separately.

**Limits:** These are two open-source stack examples, not an interchangeable or universal vehicle protocol. Actual command semantics, timing, calibration, actuator limits, diagnostics and safety mechanisms are platform and ODD dependent.

**Conditional role context â€” software developer:** conditional ADS-to-vehicle integration and interface implementation. NVIDIA and Rivian examples describe cross-subsystem/vehicle integration and diagnosis; apply only when the developer owns a command/status adapter, vehicle bring-up, interface contract or comparable integration task. The NVIDIA official posting text was search-indexed and the Rivian detail is a secondary listing mirror.

**Sources:** `D166-AUTOWARE-VEHICLE-INTERFACE-DESIGN-2026`, `D166-AUTOWARE-RAW-VEHICLE-CMD-CONVERTER-2026`, `D166-APOLLO-CHASSIS-COMMAND-SCHEMA-2026`, `D166-APOLLO-SOFTWARE-ARCH-2017`

### Integration verification must observe command-to-actuation timing, feedback, capability mismatches and degraded/manual modes

A command that is syntactically accepted is not proof that the intended vehicle behavior occurred. Integration work needs to correlate command identity/time with returned actuation and vehicle status, measure conversion and end-to-end latency, detect unsupported features, diagnose sensor/compute/vehicle faults, and define what happens on disengagement or loss of valid feedback. The component boundary may support manual override and capability reporting, but the system safety argument and test evidence remain cross-stack responsibilities. Standards recommendations and service-diagnostic interfaces can inform the test contract, but their edition, scope and adoption must be checked for the target vehicle and jurisdiction.

**Limits:** Autoware documents example capabilities and a latency measurement; ITU-T F.749.17 is scoped to purpose-built ADS-dedicated vehicles. No listed source alone defines a complete safety case, response-time budget or regulatory compliance determination.

**Conditional role context â€” software analyst:** conditional integration-test, fault-triage and release-validation task. The current software-analysis role evidence includes AV integration and quality/safety operations examples; this connection applies only to analysis/testing assignments that inspect cross-module or vehicle-level behavior, not to every software analyst role.

**Sources:** `D166-AUTOWARE-VEHICLE-INTERFACE-DESIGN-2026`, `D166-AUTOWARE-RAW-VEHICLE-CMD-CONVERTER-2026`, `D166-ITU-T-UNIVERSAL-ADS-INTERFACES-2025`, `D166-ASAM-SOVD-1-0-0`, `D166-ISO-14229-1-2026-UDS`

### Vehicle integration spans command/state interfaces, sensor-fusion services, diagnostics and safety monitoring

An ADS-to-vehicle path needs typed and time-stamped contracts: planning trajectory and localized state feed control; generic steering/speed/acceleration/jerk commands pass through a safety/command gate and vehicle adapter to platform-specific actuation; returned chassis, actuator, health and diagnostic status closes the loop. Separately, sensor performance/health/calibration inputs and synchronized time feed perception/fusion; vehicle compute middleware exposes services, communication, time sync, logging/health and diagnostics. ISO 14229 UDS addresses ECU-level diagnostic services; ASAM SOVD provides a service-oriented API for software-defined vehicle/HPC and ECU diagnostics; AUTOSAR Adaptive R25-11 documents integration of services, sensor interfaces, diagnostics and health mechanisms. ASAM OSI/XIL support simulator/testbench interfaces. These are different integration layers that can coexist; none is a universal architecture or safety proof. Correct vehicle integration therefore depends on frame/unit contracts, timestamps/latency budgets, actuator semantics, fault states, security and validated fail-safe/MRM behavior.

**Limits:** AUTOSAR/ASAM/ISO standards have edition, licensing and implementation constraints; ROS frames are project conventions; Autoware/Apollo are implementation examples. Diagnostic interfaces do not define autonomous driving behavior or certify safe actuation. Exact network, timing, safety mechanism and vehicle contract must be validated on the chosen hardware/ODD.

**Conditional role context â€” software developer:** conditional cross-component integration and vehicle interface implementation. Use where the developer owns service/interface contracts, sensor or state flow, command adapters, vehicle bring-up, diagnostic/health integration or fault handling; broad software-development titles alone do not imply automotive middleware work.

**Conditional role context â€” software analyst:** conditional interface, timing, diagnostic and regression evidence. Relevant when assigned to verify interface compatibility, command/status behavior, timing or fault/degraded-mode regression across components; does not imply all software analysts work with vehicle networks.

## D166 safety verification and validation relationships

### Verification evidence grows across scenario, software, hardware and vehicle tests; each stage answers different questions

Scenario-based virtual tests can exercise repeatable nominal, boundary and safety-critical situations at scale; MIL/SIL/HIL benches add different levels of model, software, ECU, network and hardware interaction; closed-course and on-road evidence reveal vehicle/environment effects that simulation may omit. Scenario generation and risk prioritization can be rule-based, data-driven or increasingly learned/generative, but generated cases still need plausibility, coverage and outcome checks. ASAM OSI and XIL standardize selected data/testbench interfaces that make some components or cases portable; they do not make results equivalent across simulators or prove the real-world system safe. Combine evidence by traceability to requirements, ODD, hazards and acceptance criteria, with explicit limits and residual risks.

**Limits:** Interface standards do not establish simulator realism or safety. The scenario survey is a non-peer-reviewed abstract-only preprint; the risk review is secondary evidence; regulatory requirements are jurisdiction- and vehicle/function-specific.

**Conditional role context â€” software analyst:** conditional scenario-based validation, metric design, and software/vehicle regression evidence. GM autonomy-evaluation and Waymo software-quality postings describe simulation/road evaluation, scenario or dataset coverage, statistical/ML metrics, issue triage and release evidence. Apply only where the assignment owns validation or quality analysis; postings do not prove universal duties.

**Sources:** `D166-ASAM-OSI-3-8-0`, `D166-ASAM-XIL-3-0-0`, `D166-NUPLAN-OFFICIAL-BENCHMARK`, `D166-NHTSA-ADS-CRASH-ORDER-2025`, `D166-UNECE-UNR157-ALKS`, `D166-RISK-ASSESSMENT-SURVEY-2025`, `D166-SAFETY-CRITICAL-SCENARIO-SURVEY-PREPRINT-2026`


### Automotive safety standards divide hazards, system lifecycle, scenario evaluation and approval tests

ISO 26262 addresses hazards from malfunctioning behavior in road-vehicle E/E safety-related systems; ISO 21448/SOTIF addresses unreasonable risk from functional insufficiencies or foreseeable misuse in functions that rely on complex sensing/processing, with published 2022 edition marked for revision and explicit exclusions. ISO 34502 provides a product-development scenario-based ADS safety-evaluation framework but has a limited-access-highway scope and excludes misuse, HMI and cybersecurity. ISO/DIS 34505 is still draft work on evaluating scenarios and traceably generating/prioritizing test cases for Level 3+ ADS. UN R157 addresses type approval for the narrower ALKS function, with specified track/public-road testing and fail-safe, OEDR and HMI requirements. ASAM OSI/XIL provide simulator/testbench interfaces, not a safety case. These sources fit together when applicable because they address different hazard classes, process stages or interfaces; they are not substitutes and no one standard covers every AV safety argument.

**Limits:** ISO full standards are paid and clause-level details were not inspected; ISO/DIS 34505 is draft only. UNECE type-approval obligations depend on contracting-party adoption, vehicle category and current amendment series. A standards list or conformance claim does not itself demonstrate safety or transfer competition/racing evidence to public-road deployment.

**Conditional role context â€” homologation engineer:** conditional interpretation of requirements and type-approval evidence task. Relevant where a homologation assignment translates applicable ADAS/ALKS requirements into engineering evidence and testing; do not infer that homologation owns all functional-safety engineering or that every AV role performs approval work.

**Conditional role context â€” software analyst:** conditional ADS scenario or release-validation evidence task. Relevant where a role assignment develops scenario tests, links test outcomes to requirements/ODD or supports regression/release evidence; do not infer that all software analysts own safety certification.

**Sources:** `D166-ISO-26262`, `D166-ISO-21448`, `D166-ISO-34502-SCENARIO-SAFETY-EVALUATION-2022`, `D166-ISO-DIS-34505-SCENARIO-TEST-CASE-GENERATION`, `D166-UNECE-UNR157-AMENDMENT-4-2023`, `D166-ASAM-OSI-3-8-0`, `D166-ASAM-XIL-3-0-0`


### An ADS safety case combines functional safety, SOTIF, ODD limits, scenario evidence and product-level argumentation

Safety foundations begin with vehicle/system hazards and the intended operational envelope. ISO 26262 addresses malfunctioning behavior in safety-related E/E systems; ISO 21448/SOTIF addresses unreasonable risk from functional insufficiency or foreseeable misuse involving intended functionality; ISO 34503 provides a structured ODD taxonomy, while ISO 34502 gives a bounded scenario-based ADS safety-evaluation framework and ISO/DIS 34505 is still draft work on scenario-to-test-case generation/prioritization. UL 4600 offers a technology-agnostic, goal-based safety-case approach for autonomous products without human supervision. NHTSA's current ADS guidance is voluntary and focuses on L3–L5, ODD, OEDR, fallback and other safety elements; it is not a certification or compulsory VSSA submission. These can complement each other where their scopes fit: hazard process + ODD + scenario evidence + system argument. Validation methods include requirements traceability, hazard/risk analysis, scenario selection, simulation/MIL/SIL/HIL and vehicle tests, but each evidence type has coverage and fidelity limits. A safety case makes explicit the claim, reasoning and evidence, including residual risk; one benchmark, standard or test environment cannot prove the whole claim alone.

**Limits:** Paid standards were reviewed at catalog/abstract level, not clause by clause; ISO 34505 is draft; NHTSA guidance is voluntary/U.S.-scoped; UN R157 is ALKS type-approval scoped and jurisdictionally adopted; UL 4600 is voluntary. Simulation interfaces and benchmarks do not equal a safety case or guarantee real-world safety. No one credential is established as universally required.

**Conditional role context â€” software analyst:** conditional verification planning, evidence traceability and safety-related regression task. Use when a role owns safety-related software/vehicle tests, scenario coverage, metric interpretation or release evidence; do not imply the analyst independently owns the safety case or type approval.

**Conditional role context â€” homologation engineer:** conditional market-specific compliance and approval dossier task. Use when the role translates applicable regulation/type-approval scope into vehicle requirements and test/approval evidence; distinguish that from software safety-case authorship.

**Sources:** `D166-ISO-26262`, `D166-ISO-21448`, `D166-ISO-34503-ODD-TAXONOMY-2023`, `D166-ISO-34502-SCENARIO-SAFETY-EVALUATION-2022`, `D166-ISO-DIS-34505-SCENARIO-TEST-CASE-GENERATION`, `D166-UL4600-ED3-AUTONOMOUS-SAFETY-2023`, `D166-NHTSA-ADS-VOLUNTARY-GUIDANCE-CURRENT`, `D166-ASAM-OSI-3-8-0`, `D166-ASAM-XIL-3-0-0`, `D166-NUPLAN-OFFICIAL-BENCHMARK`, `D166-NHTSA-ADS-CRASH-ORDER-2025`, `D166-UNECE-UNR157-AMENDMENT-4-2023`
